en: Agni has been awakened by the fuel of men, facing the Dawn who approaches like a milch-cow.
Like young birds springing up to the branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.
The Hotṛ-priest has been awakened for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, well-disposed, has stood upright at dawn.
The brilliant luster of the kindled one has been seen; the great god has been released from the darkness.
When he has awakened the tether of the host, the pure Agni anoints himself with pure rays of light.
Then the strength-bestowing sacrificial fee is harnessed; standing upright, he has sucked the upturned [udder] with his ladles.
The minds of those seeking the gods turn toward Agni, just as eyes converge upon the sun.
When the two Dawns of different forms give birth to him, the white steed is born at the beginning of days.
For the noble one has been born at the beginning of days; the ruddy one has been placed among the woods that have been prepared.
Bestowing seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the *hotṛ*.

Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the *hotṛ* in the fragrant lap of his mother, in her spacious place. Young, a seer, dwelling in many places, true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), he is the sustainer of the peoples, kindled even in their midst.

Now they indeed magnify with prostrations that inspired sage, the efficient Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, at the sacrifices— He who has spread himself across the two worlds by the Eternal Law; they groom the prize-winner with clarified butter.
The one worthy of grooming is groomed in his own home, the domestic lord, praised by seers, our auspicious guest.
The bull with a thousand horns, whose strength is such, O Agni, has by his power cast all others aside. O Agni, you instantly surpass all others for him to whom you have become most beautiful—
worthy of praise, wondrous, radiant, the beloved guest of human clans.
To you, O youngest Agni, the peoples bring tribute from near and from afar.
Take notice of the most praiseworthy man’s devotion; great and auspicious is your vast protection, O Agni.
Today, O radiant Agni, mount your shining chariot together with those worthy of sacrifice.
Knowing the paths, bring the gods here to this wide mid-air to eat the oblation.
We have spoken a word of praise to the wise, worthy of sacrifice, the bull, the vigorous one.
Gaviṣṭhira has fixed his hymn with reverence upon Agni, like a far-reaching golden ornament set in heaven.
The young mother carries the boy, firmly enclosed within her secret place; she does not yield him to the father.
O people, they behold his face, unchanging, placed before them upon the fire-wood.
O young woman, who is this boy that you, the handmaid, carry? The queen has given birth to him.
RV_05.002.02.2 For many autumns the embryo has grown; I beheld him born when his mother gave birth.
RV_05.002.03.1 I saw from afar, from my field, one with golden teeth and bright color, fashioning his weapons.
RV_05.002.03.2 Having bestowed upon him the immortal, purified [soma], what can those who lack Indra and are devoid of hymns do to me?
From the field I saw him wandering far away, like a well-nourished herd, shining intensely.
They did not seize him, for he had been born; even those who were grey-haired become young women again.
Who are they that separate my young bull from the cattle—those whose guardian was never a stranger?
RV_05.002.05.2 May those who have seized him release him; may he, being wise, drive the cattle toward us.

RV_05.002.06.1 The enemies have hidden the King of the dwelling, the abode of people, among mortals. RV_05.002.06.2 May the sacred prayers of Atri release him; let the revilers become objects of reproach themselves.
Even Śunaḥśepa, who had been bound and cast down from the sacrificial post, you released from a thousand bonds, for he had performed his service.
In this very way, O Agni, loosen our bonds; O wise Hotṛ, sit here and release us. For you went away from me in anger; the protector of the gods' laws has declared this to me.
Indra, the knowing one, has indeed looked out for you; instructed by him, O Agni, I have come here.
Agni shines with his lofty light; he makes all things manifest through his greatness.
He overcomes the godless, malevolent illusions; he sharpens his two horns to gore the Rakṣasa.
And let the roars of Agni rise to heaven, with sharp weapons to slay the Rakṣasa. Even in his exhilaration, his splendors shatter [the foe]; the godless obstructors cannot hold him back.
O many-born one, I, the inspired singer, have fashioned this hymn for you, as a skillful craftsman fashions a chariot.
If you, O divine Agni, should accept this, may we win through these waters that possess the light of heaven.
The bull with the thick neck, growing strong, shall gather the wealth of the enemy without a foe.
Thus have the immortals spoken to this Agni; may he grant protection to the man who spreads the sacrificial grass, may he grant protection to the man who offers oblations.
O Agni, you are born as Varuṇa; when kindled, you become Mitra. In you, O Son of Strength, dwell all the gods; you are Indra for the mortal who offers oblations.
You become Aryaman when it concerns maidens, for you bear their secret name, O self-dependent one.
They anoint Mitra, well-established, as it were with milk, when you make the husband and wife of one mind.
For your glory, O Rudra, the Maruts groom themselves, for that birth of yours is beautiful and wondrous.
That footprint of Viṣṇu which was established as the highest—by that you guard the secret name of the cows.
By your splendor, O beautiful god, the gods, bestowing much [upon you], attained immortality.
Men have established Agni as the Hotṛ-priest; desiring his favor, the yearning ones have offered praise for the sake of the living man.
O Agni, no priest before you has been more skilled in sacrifice; none surpasses you in wisdom, O self-dependent lord.
And that man in whose house you become a guest, O God, shall overcome mortals through sacrifice. O Agni, protected by you, may we, seeking wealth and awakening with our oblation,
overcome mortals in the contest, in the assemblies of days, and through riches, O Son of Strength.
RV_05.003.07.1 Whoever brings sin or offense against us—place that evil upon the one who intends evil.
RV_05.003.07.2 O wise Agni, strike down this curse of the man who injures us with duplicity.
RV_05.003.08.1 At the dawning of this light, O God, the ancients, making you their messenger, worshipped you with oblations.
When you, O Agni, go forth at the assembly of riches, a god kindled by mortals together with the Vasus;
Protect the father, fight as one who knows, O Son of Strength, for the son who honors you.
When, O wise one, will you look upon us? O Agni, when, as a knower of Truth, will you set us right?
The father, O Vasu, bestows many names upon you as he offers praise, if you should take pleasure in them.
Will not Agni, increasing in strength and longing for the power of the god, win favor?
O most youthful Agni, you indeed carry your singer across all difficulties.
Thieves have been seen; men who are enemies have appeared, their intentions unknown, full of guile. These journeys have turned toward you; indeed, this sin has been confessed before you, O Vasu.
This Agni shall not deliver us over to reproach, nor to the one who seeks to harm us, for he grows ever stronger.
O Agni, King, I rejoice in you, the lord of riches among all treasures, during the sacrifices.
Through you, may we who strive for booty win the prize; may we overcome the hostile attacks of mortals.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, our ageless father, is pervasive, far-shining, and beautiful to behold for us.
With a well-tended household fire, shine forth toward us with nourishment; measure out for us glorious renown.

The sage of the clans, the lord of human tribes, the pure, the purifier, Agni whose back is anointed with ghee—him you have established as the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest; he wins desirable boons among the gods.
O Agni, being in harmony with the *iḷā* offering, take pleasure [in it], striving together with the rays of the sun.
O Jātavedas, enjoy our fuel and bring the gods here to eat the oblation. Being beloved as the domestic master and the guest in the house, come to this our sacrifice, you who are wise.
O Agni, having struck down all assailants, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies.
Drive away the Dasyu with your weapon, creating strength for your own body. Since you, O Son of Strength, satisfy the gods, therefore, O most heroic Agni, protect us in the contest for booty.
O Agni, may we worship you with hymns; may we worship you with oblations, O Purifier of auspicious luster.
Send to us wealth containing all boons; bestow upon us all riches.
O Agni, Son of Strength, dweller in the three abodes, take pleasure in our sacrifice and in our offering.
May we be doers of good deeds among the gods; protect us with your triple-layered shelter.
O Jātavedas, carry us across all difficulties as one crosses a river by boat;
O Agni, being praised with homage like Atri, be the protector of our bodies.
O Jātavedas, I, a mortal, calling upon you, the immortal, with a humble heart, beseech you: bestow glory upon us; may I attain immortality through my offspring, O Agni.
To whichever doer of good deeds you, O Jātavedas Agni, create a pleasant dwelling place—
RV_05.004.11.2 He attains wealth consisting of horses, sons, heroes, and cattle for his well-being.
RV_05.005.00.11 Offer sharp clarified butter to the well-kindled, radiant flame.
RV_05.005.00.12 To Agni Jātavedas.
May Narāśaṃsa, the invincible one, prepare this sacrifice;
for he is the sage with honeyed hands.
O Agni, being invoked, bring hither the wonderful and beloved Indra.
With easy-moving chariots, come for our aid!
O you who are soft as wool, spread yourself out; the hymns have resounded in your praise. O radiant one, become ours for the sake of gain!
O divine Doors, open yourselves for our protection, providing easy access;
further and further extend the sacrifice.
The two young Mothers of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), of beautiful countenance, who increase our vital strength.
We pray for the evening and the dawn.
O two divine Hotṛ-priests of man, invoked upon the flight of the wind,
come to this our sacrifice.

May Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī—the three goddesses who bring delight—sit upon the sacrificial grass, they who are unfailing. O Tvaṣṭṛ, come here, auspicious one; you are the pervasive nourisher, both by yourself and through your own power.
At every sacrifice,
protect us. O Lord of the Forest, wherever you know the secret names of the gods, there bring our oblations.
Svāhā to Agni and Varuṇa! Svāhā to Indra and the Maruts! Svāhā to the gods, the oblation!
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home;
to whom the swift horses go home, and to whom the constant prize-winners go home. Bring nourishment to the singers!
He is that Agni who is praised as the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows come together, and the swift-running steeds, and the well-born patrons; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
For Agni, the lord of all people, bestows a prize-winning steed upon the clan.
O Agni, for the sake of wealth, he who is self-sustaining goes toward what is desirable; being well-pleased, bring nourishment to those who praise you.
O Agni, we kindle your radiant and undecaying light, O God, so that this most wondrous fuel of yours may shine in heaven; bring nourishment to those who praise you.
To thee, O Agni, with a *ṛc*-verse is offered the oblation, O Lord of the bright flame!
O most radiant one, wondrous Lord of the people, bearer of the sacrificial food, for thee it is poured; bring nourishment to thy praisers!
These Agnis have shone forth among the fires; they cause all that is desirable to flourish.
RV 5.6.6.2: They have been urged forward, they have been sent forth; they hasten on in succession. Bring nourishment to those who praise you! RV 5.6.7.1:
O Agni, those flames of yours have grown great like powerful steeds.
RV 5.6.7.2: They who with the leaps of their hooves burst open the stalls of cattle—bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Agni, bring new provisions and secure dwellings to us who praise you.
May we be those who have sung your praises, having you as our messenger in every house; bring nourishment to those who laud you.
O most radiant one, you mix both ladles of clarified butter within your mouth.
And so, O Lord of Might, fill us up during our hymns; bring nourishment to those who praise you.
Thus have they ever honored the ageless Agni with songs and sacrifices in due order.
May he bestow upon us great heroic strength and that abundance of swift horses; bring nourishment to those who praise you.
O friends, bring together for Agni— him who is the highest among the peoples, the son of strength, the mighty— one who is directed toward you with food and hymns of praise.
Wherever his assembly may be, men rejoice in the gathering of heroes.
Even the worthy ones kindle him; living beings bring him to birth.
When we gather together the sacrificial foods and the oblations of men, he seizes the rein of the glorious power of Truth.
He indeed makes his banner visible even at night for one who stays afar;
when he, the purifier, the ageless one, consumes the lords of the forest.
He in whose service they pour out sweat upon the paths.
Truly, they have mounted him, the one worthy of noble kinship, as if upon the back of the earth— him,
the mortal who is desired by many, whom he has established for the sustenance of all,
the sweetener of nourishments, and the protector even for the living man.
For he indeed, like a beast, mows down the desert land;
golden-bearded, bright-toothed, a skillful craftsman of undiminished power.
Truly pure is he, from whom [the soma] flows forth like an axe, as it did for Atri.
The mother has given birth well, for she, acting with skill, has attained her portion.
O Agni, you to whom the clarified butter is poured, may that which is yours be auspicious for our nourishment.
Bestow upon these mortals splendor, fame, and wisdom.

Thus, O impetuous one, I have taken away the fury that you bestowed upon him as his cattle; now, O Agni, may Atri overcome the Dasyus who do not give, and may he overcome those men who withhold our food.
O Agni, those seeking the Truth, the ancient ones, have kindled you, the ancient one, for the sake of aid, O you who are strengthened by power.
The one who shines manifold, the worshipful, the all-sustaining, the friend of the house, the master of the home, the most excellent.
O Agni, the clans have established you as their ancient guest, the flame-haired master of the home;
you whose banner is lofty, who possess many forms, who win the wealth, who grant good protection, who provide good help, and who consume the aged foe.
RV_05.008.03.1 O Agni, the human tribes praise you, the knower of the sacrificial office, the discerning one, the greatest bestower of treasures.
RV_05.008.03.2 You who dwell in the secret place, O fortunate one, visible to all, loud-sounding, worthy of fair sacrifice, and resplendent with clarified butter.
RV_05.008.04.1 To you, O Agni, the sustainer, we have always drawn near with our songs, praising you with reverence.
Being kindled, O Aṅgiras, as a god, take pleasure in us with your glorious and beautiful radiance, you who belong to the mortal man.
O Agni, manifold in form, you bestow vital strength upon every clan as of old, O much-praised one.
You rule over many foods by your power; that brilliance of yours, when it blazes forth, is not to be assailed.
O Agni, most youthful one, when you were kindled, the gods made you their messenger, the bearer of oblations;
they established you—wide-striding, having ghee as your womb, invoked with offerings—as a brilliant eye that impels the thought.
O Agni, from of old, those seeking favor have kindled you with good fuel, you who are invoked with ghee.
Growing strong, nourished by the plants, you spread yourself abroad across the earthly expanses.
O Agni, mortals bearing oblations invoke you, the god;
I acknowledge you as Jātavedas, for you shall carry the offerings in due order.
Agni is the Hotṛ-priest of the bountiful dwelling where the sacrificial grass is trimmed;
he is the one toward whom all sacrifices proceed, and all strengths that seek renown.
And him, as the Araṇi produced him like a newborn infant.
Agni, the sustainer of the human tribes, the performer of the perfect sacrifice;
And indeed, you are difficult to seize, like the son of those who wander.
O Agni, you who burn many forests, like a beast in a pasture.
And now, his smoky flames come together completely;
when Trita blows upon him in heaven like a smith, he sharpens him as a smith does.
O Agni, through your protections and through the praises of Mitra—
May we, free from hatred, overcome the misfortunes caused by mortals. O Agni, bring that wealth to us, O powerful one, for these men.
May he protect us and nourish us; may he be the winner of booty. And stand by us for our increase in battles.
O Agni, bring us most powerful splendor, O irresistible one! Open for us a path to wealth and abundance for the sake of strength.
O wonderful Agni, you [are] ours through wisdom and the greatness of your power.

In you, the power of the Asuras has ascended; acting as such, you are worthy of sacrifice like Mitra. O Agni, increase for us the household and the prosperity of these men, the patrons who, through their hymns of praise, have attained great riches.
O Agni, those men who adorn their songs for you, O radiant one, bestowing horses as their gift—
those vigorous heroes with their own powers, whose great fame awakens by itself even from heaven. O Agni, those brilliant flames of yours go forth boldly, shining.
Like lightning flashing all around, like the roar of a chariot seeking booty—
Now, O Agni, come for our protection and for the granting of gifts to us;
And may our patrons cross over all the quarters of the earth.

O Agni Aṅgiras, you who have been praised and are being lauded, bring to us, O Hotṛ, wealth that overcomes the mighty, for the sake of our praisers and for your own glory; and stand up for our increase in battles.
The watchful guardian of the people, Agni, the highly skillful, has been born for new-found prosperity.
With a face of ghee, the pure one shines brilliantly with great splendor that touches the heavens for the sake of the Bharatas.
Men have kindled Agni—the banner of sacrifice, the first domestic priest—in his threefold seat.
Seated upon the sacrificial grass on the same chariot as Indra and the gods, he, the wise Hotṛ, sits down for the performance of the sacrifice.
Unrubbed, you are born pure from your two mothers; as a delightful sage, you have arisen from Vivasvat.
They strengthened you with clarified butter, O Agni, when you were invoked; your smoke became a banner resting in heaven.
May Agni come straightway to our sacrifice; men carry Agni forth from house to house.
Agni became the messenger, the bearer of oblations; choosing Agni, they choose him who possesses the wisdom of a seer.
O Agni, let this most honey-sweet speech be for you; let this inspired thought be a blessing to your heart.
As great rivers fill the ocean, so do our songs fill you with power and increase you in strength.

RV 5.11.6.1: O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered you, who were hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest. 6.2: You are born when being churned with great force; they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
RV 5.12.1.1: To the lofty Agni, the worthy of sacrifice, the bull of Truth, the Asura, let us offer our prayer.
Like clarified butter well-purified at the sacrifice, I offer this song directed toward the Bull.
O Knower of Truth, take note of Truth; pierce open the many streams of Truth!
I do not serve the sorcerer by force nor by duplicity; I serve the Truth of the ruddy Bull.

By what means, O Agni, acting according to *ṛta* through *ṛta*, do you become the knower of our new hymn? The god knows for me the seasons, he who guards the seasons; I am not the master of this wealth that wins it.
Who, O Agni, are your bonds for the enemy? Who are your brilliant protectors who shall win [the prize]?
RV_05.012.04.2 Who, O Agni, drink the nourishment of falsehood? Who are the guardians of the speech of the wicked?

RV_05.012.05.1 These friends of thine, O Agni, have turned away; though they were once auspicious, they have become inauspicious. RV_05.012.05.2 They have harmed themselves by their own words, speaking crooked things to one who acts with rectitude.

RV 5.12.6.1: O Agni, he who honors your sacrifice with reverence protects the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull. 6.2: May his dwelling be broad and successful; may the lineage of Nahuṣa, as he spreads forth, prosper.
RV 5.13.1.1: Singing praises, we invoke you; singing praises, we kindle you.
O Agni, we sing praises for your protection. O Agni, we fashion today an effective hymn of praise for you who touch the heavens,
desiring wealth from the god.
May Agni, who is the Hotṛ among men, take pleasure in our songs; may he worship the divine host. O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and choice-worthy Hotṛ.
Through you they spread out the sacrifice.
O Agni, the inspired singers increase you, who are most excellent at winning booty and well-praised;
grant us great heroic strength.
O Agni, as the felly encompasses the spokes, so do you encompass the gods;
you strive for wondrous wealth.
Awakening the immortal Agni with a hymn of praise, kindling him with fuel.
May he place our oblations among the gods. Mortals invoke him, the immortal god, at the sacrifices—
the best of sacrificers among the human race.
For him indeed all constantly invoke with the ladle dripping with clarified butter— the god Agni, that he may carry their oblations.
Agni, once born, shone forth, slaying the Dasyus and dispelling darkness with his light.
He found the cattle, the waters, and the light.
Worship Agni, the seer worthy of invocation, whose back is anointed with clarified butter;
may he come and hear my call.
They have strengthened Agni, who belongs to all people, with clarified butter, with hymns,
and with well-intentioned, eloquent words.
I offer a song of praise to the wise, renowned, and ancient ordainer, the one worthy of glory.
The Asura Agni, well-disposed, is seated upon the clarified butter; he is the sustainer of wealth and the supporter of all treasures.
By means of Truth they have established Truth as the foundation, through the power of sacrifice in the highest heaven.
Seated upon the support of heaven according to its law, those who have attained the unborn by means of the born.
Seeking to remove distress, they extend their bodies; great and invincible is the vitality for the Ancient One.
May he, newly born, overcome the enclosures; they stand around him on all sides like a provoked lion.
When, spreading out like a mother, you bear every person for their nourishment and for their vision.
From age to age, assuming thy form for the sake of decay, thou goest about in thy own person, taking on various shapes.
May strength now protect the limit of thy power; O God, grant us a wide, flowing, and sustaining stream of wealth.
Like a thief concealing his tracks in a secret place, thou hast reached Atri, making him mindful of great riches.
Sing forth a great song of praise to the radiant god Agni, whom mortals have placed in the forefront like Mitra with their hymns of glorification— he who, by his days,
has become the Hotṛ-priest of men through the strength of Dakṣa’s arms.
Agni conveys the oblation in due order, like Bhaga bestowing a desirable boon.
In the praise-song of this liberal patron, in the friendship of him whose flame has grown strong— in whom, the loud-sounding noble one, all [the gods] have placed their vigor.
For now, O Agni, through the greatness of their excellent heroic power— even the two worlds have not encompassed his fame, as if he were a youth.
Now come to us, O Agni; being praised, bring us what is desirable.
RV_05.016.05.2 May we and those who are our patrons secure well-being together; and do thou stand with us for our increase in battles.
RV_05.017.01.1 Thus, O mortal man, with sacrifices, one should invoke Agni, the most powerful god, for protection at the well-performed rite.
RV_05.017.01.2 Puru has invoked Agni for aid when the self-sustaining sacrifice has been prepared.

For by his own mouth you are considered most glorious in your domain; him, the vault of heaven with wondrous luster, the delightful one, [we praise] beyond our thought. His garment indeed is light, he who has been yoked by impetuous song.
Whose flames blaze mightily with seed like that of heaven;
by the will of this wise wonder-worker, wealth comes upon his chariot.
Thus Agni, who is to be invoked among all the clans, is praised.
RV_05.017.05.1 Now indeed, through our mouths, the wise patrons shall obtain what is desirable.
RV_05.017.05.2 O Son of Strength, protect us for our aid; be able for our well-being, and stand up for our increase in battles.
RV_05.018.01.1 At dawn let Agni, the much-beloved guest of the people, be praised.
He who, being immortal, delights in all the oblations among mortals— To him,

the one who from of old carries away what is injured, through the greatness of his own skill, he, the immortal one, bestows the soma-drop in due succession; even your praiser [attains it], O Immortal.

I call upon him for you with a song— he whose flame is long-lived, among the wealthy patrons, whose chariot moves unhurt, O giver of horses. Those in whom there is brilliant insight, who guard the hymns of praise.

The sacred grass is strewn for Svarṇara; they have established glorious deeds around it. O Agni, grant resplendent, great, and lofty fame to those patrons who have given me fifty horses at the joint-praise, O immortal one—fame that is heroic among men.
The various forms are brought forth; from the covering, the covering has become manifest. He gazes upon the lap of his mother.
Discerning, they have offered oblations; with unblinking eyes, they guard their manly power.
They have entered the firm fortress.
The people of Śvaitreya, the tribes, have increased in splendor; Bṛhaduktha, with a golden necklace around his neck, is like one seeking booty through this sweet draught.
Like beloved, desirable milk, he is the stranger together with the kinsmen;
like a cauldron filled with strength, he is undeceived and the deceiver of many.
Playing, O beam of light, come to us, finding kinship with the wind and the ashes.
RV_05.019.05.2 These [flames] of his are like sharp, well-sharpened spears; they stand upon the breast, dwelling in the chest.
RV_05.20.01.1 O Agni, best winner of booty, whatever wealth you yourself deem worthy, RV_05.20.01.2 that, through our songs, make famous among the gods as a praiseworthy companion for us.
O Agni, those who do not lead away from the man— those who have grown strong through thy fierce power— they turn away from the hatred and the guile of him who follows another's law.
We choose thee as the Hotṛ-priest, O Agni, the accomplisher of skill.
At the sacrifices, we who offer oblations invoke with our song the ancient one.
Thus, O powerful one, so that day by day you may be for our aid—for wealth and for the Truth—O wise one, may we be sharers of the feast with cattle; may we be sharers of the feast with heroes.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee.
O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
For thou, O Agni, art well-pleased and kindled among the human folk.
The ladles approach you in succession, O well-born one, you who are anointed with clarified butter.
All the gods, acting in harmony, have made you their messenger. Serving you, O sage, they invoke you as a god at the sacrifices.
RV_05.021.04.1 Let the mortal worship Agni, your god, with a sacrifice to the gods.
RV_05.021.04.2 Being kindled, O bright one, shine forth; sit upon the seat of Ṛta, sit upon the seat of the sacrificial food.
RV_05.022.01.1 Like Atri, sing forth, O Viśvasāman, to him whose flame is purifying.
He who is to be praised at the sacrifices, the most delightful Hotṛ among the people—
place Agni Jātavedas down, the divine officiating priest. May the sacrifice proceed today in due order, most capacious for the gods.

O Agni, the mortals, seeking your aid, have meditated upon you, the god of discerning mind. Desiring your most excellent protection, we have called upon you. O powerful Agni, take heed of this our speech.
O Lord of the Household, fair of cheek, the Atris strengthen you with hymns; the Atris beautify you with songs of praise.
O Agni, by your victorious might, bring us wealth that overcomes all people, so that we may prevail in battles for booty.
O Agni, bring hither that wealth which overcomes hostile armies,
for you are the true and wondrous giver of booty consisting of cattle. For all people, with one accord, having spread the sacrificial grass, [invoke] you.
They approach the beloved Hotṛ in his dwellings for many desirable boons.
For he, the one who belongs to all people, has established his power against the assailant.
O Agni, in these dwellings, shine for us like wealth, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier!

O Agni, be our closest friend, our protector, and our auspicious refuge. Agni, the Vasu, renowned for wealth, come hither and grant us most resplendent riches. As such, take heed of us and hear our call; deliver us from every malicious person.
To you, O most radiant one, O shining one, we now pray for the welfare of our friends.
I shall sing toward Agni, the god, for your protection; may he, the possessor of wealth, grant us riches.
May the son of the *ṛṣis*, the upholder of *ṛta*, bestow gifts and carry us across our enemies.
For he is the true one, whom the ancients and even the gods kindled—
the Hotṛ-priest with the pleasant tongue, rich in splendor through his brilliant lights. May he [favor] us with our most extensive meditation and with his most excellent benevolence.
O Agni, worthy of choice, shine wealth upon us through our well-fashioned hymns.
Agni reigns among the gods; Agni enters among mortals.
Agni is our bearer of oblations; honor Agni with your prayers.

Agni gives to the donor a son who is most highly renowned, a supreme priest of great prayer, unconquered, and a lord who makes himself heard. Agni gives a true master who, with his men, has conquered in battle.
Agni is the steed that rushes swiftly, the conqueror who is never defeated.
O Vibhāvasu, sing a lofty hymn to Agni with that which is most effective for him.
Like a sovereign queen, wealth and spoils of war rise up from you.

Your brilliant rays resound mightily like the sound of pressing-stones; and your roar has gone forth of its own accord from heaven like thunder. Thus, seeking wealth, we have paid homage to Agni, the powerful one.
May he, the one of excellent wisdom, carry us across all hostilities as if with a boat.
O Agni, Purifier, with your radiant and pleasant tongue, O God,
bring the gods hither and worship them.
We pray to you, O you whose back is dripping with ghee, O you of brilliant luster, who look upon the light of heaven; bring the gods here for the feast.
O Sage, we kindle you, the radiant one, whose sacrifice is welcomed.
O Agni, [raise] the great [song] at the sacrifice. O Agni, come with all the gods for the giving of the oblation;
we choose you as the Hotṛ-priest.
O Agni, bring heroic strength to the sacrificer who presses the soma;
sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass.
Being kindled, O Agni, victor of thousands, you nourish the sacred ordinances.
The praiseworthy messenger of the gods.
Set down Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the youngest,
the divine officiating priest.
Let the sacrifice proceed in due order today, most spacious for the gods;
spread the sacrificial grass for them to sit upon.
May the Maruts, the Aśvins, Mitra, and Varuṇa sit here.
O gods, with your entire host!
The lord of the virtuous has bestowed upon me two oxen drawn by a cart; the most wise Asura among the wealthy is he.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivr̥ṣan, has distinguished himself with ten thousand gifts.

He who gives me a hundred and twenty cows and two bay steeds, well-yoked and easy to drive— O Vaiśvānara Agni, being well-praised and increasing in strength, grant protection to Tryaruṇa. Thus, O Agni, desiring your favor, Trasadasyu has offered this newest song to you, the most recent one.
Tryaruṇa, who with his disciplined mind praises my many ancient songs as one born of great power;
He who proclaims "May he [grant] to me" for the sake of the wise Aśvamedha—
Granting gain to the one who approaches with a hymn, granting wisdom to the one who follows the *ṛta*.
He whose hundred dappled bulls rouse me up,
the gifts of Aśvamedha, like three-headed Soma-stalks;
O Indra and Agni, [grant] great heroic power at the hundred-giving Aśvamedha.
Maintain a lofty dominion, like the unaging sun in heaven.
Kindled, Agni has sent his flame to the sky; facing the Dawn, he shines far and wide.
Turning eastward, she who possesses all boons goes forth with salutations, praising the gods with an oblation of clarified butter.
Being kindled, you reign as the king of immortality; you attend to the one who prepares the oblation for his well-being.
He whom you impel gains all wealth; O Agni, you establish him as a guest of honor before [the gods].
O Agni, exert your strength for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent.
Make the lordship of the household easy to govern; trample down the powers of those who act as enemies. O Agni, I praise the splendor of you, the greatly kindled one;
you are a bull, full of luster, and you are kindled at the sacrifices.
O Agni, kindled and invoked with oblations, sacrifice to the gods at this well-performed rite;
for you are the bearer of the sacrificial offerings. Offer the oblation and honor Agni as the sacrifice proceeds.
Choose him as the bearer of oblations.
Aryaman [upholds] three for man in the assembly of the gods; they maintain the three celestial luminaries.
The Maruts, pure in will, sing your praises; you, O Indra, are their wise seer.

When the Maruts sang their praise to Indra, who was exhilarated after drinking of the pressed soma, he seized his thunderbolt and struck the dragon; he released the mighty waters to flow. And you, O Maruts, are my spiritual powers (*brahmāṇaḥ*); may Indra drink of this well-pressed soma.
For that offering found the cattle for Manu; having drunk of it, Indra slew the serpent.
Then he propped the two worlds far apart; though he had wrapped himself around them, he struck the beast with fear.
Indra, casting away the devourer, struck down the Dānava who was panting against him.

Then, O Maghavan, by your wisdom all the gods yielded to you the drinking of Soma, when you brought down the flying bay mares of Sūrya that were in front, before Etaśa. When Maghavan simultaneously shattered his ninety-nine coils with the thunderbolt.
RV_05.029.06.2 Praising Indra in the assembly, the Maruts with a *triṣṭubh* hymn forced open the sky.
RV_05.029.07.1 As a friend for his friend, Agni quickly cooked three hundred buffaloes by means of his power (*kratvā*).
RV_05.029.07.2 Together, Indra drank three lakes of pressed Soma from Manu for the slaying of Vṛtra.

When Maghavan drank three hundred buffaloes’ worth of Soma and three lakes of it, all the gods raised a shout of praise for Indra, as if for a victory, because he had slain the serpent. When you, O Indra, went to Uśanas’s house with your swift, powerful horses, you came with those steeds that gallop at will.
RV 5.29.9: Victorious here, you went forth on the same chariot with Kutsa; with the gods, you indeed overthrew Śuṣṇa. RV 5.29.10:
You tore away one wheel of Sūrya’s chariot; for Kutsa, you made the other path wide enough for him to travel.
You crushed the noseless Dasyus with your weapon and cast down those of malicious speech into their own dwelling.
The hymns of Gaurivīti magnified you; you delivered Pipru over to Vaidathina.
Ṛjiśvan chose you for friendship; cooking sacrificial cakes, he drank his soma.
The Navagvas and Daśagvas, having pressed the soma, honor Indra with their songs of praise.
RV 5.29.12 Even the stall of cattle, though it was enclosed, the men, exerting themselves, threw open.
RV 5.29.13 How indeed, O Maghavan, shall I describe to you, as one who knows, the heroic deeds which you have performed?
And those new ones which you, O Most Mighty One, shall now perform—let us proclaim them forth among the assemblies.
O Indra, you have performed all these many deeds from your birth, irresistible by virtue of your heroism.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, whatever you, bold as you are, shall now perform—there is no one to resist that power of yours.
O most powerful Indra, take pleasure in the prayers being offered; we have fashioned for you those new hymns which are yours, O mightiest one.
Like two auspicious, well-fashioned garments for one seeking wealth, I, the skillful craftsman, have fashioned [you] like a chariot.

Where is that hero? Who has seen Indra, approaching on his easy-rolling chariot with his two bay horses—he who, wielding the thunderbolt and desiring the pressed soma, comes as a much-invoked guest to that dwelling with his aid?
I have proclaimed his secret, powerful station, seeking to follow the track of the one who laid it down.
I asked others, and they said to me, "May we, as men awakened, attain Indra.
Now, at the pressing of the juice, let us proclaim those deeds of yours, O Indra, which you have performed and which you have graciously accepted from us.
The ignorant man may learn from it, and the wise man may hear it; this Maghavan, with his entire host, carries it away.
O Indra, as soon as you were born, you made your mind firm; desiring battle, you alone went against even the many.
By your might, you split even the rock with your lightning-flash and found the enclosure of the ruddy cows.
When you, the supreme one, were born in the highest distance, bearing a name renowned afar—from that very Indra the gods were struck with fear; he conquered all the waters whose lord was the Dāsa.
For you alone these most gracious Maruts sing their hymn of praise; they press out the Soma juice.
Indra overcame with his wondrous powers the guileful Ahi, who had hidden himself and was lying in wait for the waters.
O Maghavan, impelling the gift from birth, you struck down the obstructors, desiring to gather the cattle.
There, seeking a path for Manu, you rolled off the head of the Dāsa Namuci.
For you have made me your ally, O Indra, while you were crushing the head of the Dāsa Namuci. Like a whirling stone, you cast both heaven and earth apart for the Maruts.
For the Dāsa has made women his weapons; what can his feeble armies do to me?
For he beheld both his milch-cows within; then Indra went forth to battle against the Dasyu. Here the cows lowed together on every side, having been separated here and there from their calves.
Indra reunited them by his powers when the well-pressed Soma juices exhilarated him.
When the brown, stirred Soma drops exhilarated him, the Bull roared aloud at his dwellings. Having drunk of this, Indra, the breaker of forts, gave back the ruddy cows.
The Ruśamas have performed this auspicious deed, O Agni, giving four thousand cattle.
RV 5.30.12. We have accepted the offered gifts of Ṛṇaṃcaya, the most heroic among men.
RV 5.30.13.1. The Ruśamas, O Agni, have sent me home well-adorned with thousands of cattle.
RV 5.30.13.2. At the dawning of the night’s end, the strong pressed juices have exhilarated Indra.
That night, the one that was to end, dawned for Ṛṇaṃcaya, the king of the Ruśamas. Like a swift, prize-winning steed urged on, Babhru won four thousand [cattle].
O Agni, we have received four thousand head of cattle from among the Ruśamas.
RV 5.30.15: Even the heated cauldron that was made of iron for the Pravargya rite—that we sages have taken up.
RV 5.31.1: Indra, the Bountiful One, makes a downward slope for the chariot upon which he has mounted, as it strives for booty.
RV 5.31.2: Like a herdsman driving cattle to the herd, he opens the way; uninjured and seeking to win, he goes as the foremost.
Come hither, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; do not be reluctant. O you who bestow golden gifts, be with us.
For there is nothing better than you, O Indra; even those who were born have you made subject to your will.
When his power was born from strength, Indra manifested all his divine powers.
He impelled the well-yielding cows within the cave; with light he rolled away the encompassing darkness.
The Anus fashioned a chariot for thy horse; Tvaṣṭṛ, O much-invoked one, fashioned the radiant thunderbolt.
The priests, magnifying Indra with hymns, strengthened him for the slaying of the serpent.
RV_05.031.05.1 When the strong ones sang their hymn of praise to you, the strong one, O Indra— the pressing-stones and Aditi being of one accord—
RV_05.031.05.2 The wheel-rims, though without horses and without chariots, sped forth against the Dasyus, impelled by Indra.
RV_05.031.06.1 I shall proclaim your former deeds, O Maghavan, and those recent ones which you have performed.
When you, by your power, upheld both heaven and earth, winning for Manu the waters that were wondrous in their bounty.
This indeed was your deed, O wonder-worker, O sage: when slaying the serpent, you measured out your strength therein.
You seized even the magic wiles of Śuṣṇa; advancing, you drove away the Dasyus.
O Indra, you stayed the well-flowing waters for Yadu and Turvaśa on the far shore.
You went forth with fierce power; you brought Kutsa along when the gods and Uśanā met together.
O Indra and Kutsa, as you travel upon your chariot, let your horses carry you even to our ear.
You blew her away from the waters, away from her dwelling; you drove the darkness from the heart of the liberal patron.
Seeking aid, even this seer has come to the well-yoked horses of Vāta who are already harnessed.
In this matter, O Indra, all the Maruts were your friends; the sacred hymns increased your power.

Even the Sun, in the race for the prize, placed his chariot behind the one who sped forward; Etaśa brought the wheel and brings it back; placing it in front, he shall grant us wisdom. He has come, O people, that Indra may behold him; seeking his friend who has pressed the Soma, he has gone to him.
The pressing-stone speaks as it is brought to the altar, for whose sake the Adhvaryu priests move swiftly.
Those mortals who have been pleased, O Immortal One—let them not fall into distress; they have indeed been pleased.
Praise those who offer sacrifice, and bestow vigor upon those people among whom we may dwell.
You burst open the spring; you released the channels; you set free the obstructed floods.
O Indra, when you shattered the great mountain, you let loose the streams and struck down the Dānava.
You, O wielder of the thunderbolt, hastened the well that was obstructed by the seasons, the udder of the mountain.
O fierce Indra, having struck down even the serpent Ahi as he lay prostrate, you established your own power.
Indra, with his might, struck down the deadly weapon of that very great beast. He who alone was considered matchless—surely another, even stronger than him, has been born from him.
Even him who rejoices in his own power, the son of the mist, the well-growing one who goes into the darkness—

him the wielder of the thunderbolt, with his impetuous onset, struck down Śuṣṇa, the fury of the Dānava, with his bolt. Even him who sat there by his wiles, though he was thought invulnerable, he indeed found his vital spot.
When you, O Lord of good dominion, provided him with a full draught of the exhilarating juice while he was eager for battle in the darkness of his dwelling;
when you, O Bull, exhilarated by the pressed soma, raised your hand aloft and struck down even him who lay there like a mere speck, increasing in might within the sunless darkness.
When Indra raised his irresistible weapon against the great Dānava, he struck him down;
when he dealt him a blow at the hurling of the thunderbolt, he cast him to the lowest depth of all living beings.
The fierce one seized for himself that very wave, the honey-drinker who lay there, the unyielding enclosure.
With a great weapon, he struck down the footless devourer in his own dwelling, the one who speaks with delusion.
Who can withstand his fury and his might? He alone, unopposed, carries off the spoils of wealth. Even these two goddesses, the expanses of heaven, flee in fear of Indra’s power.
The divine axe has bent down before him; for Indra, the path has opened like one longing [for him].
When he gathers all power together with these [fingers], the peoples bow down before him, the self-dependent one.
I hear of you alone, the lord of the people, born as the protector of the five tribes, renowned among men.
RV 5.32.11: Him, the newest one, the eager ones have grasped for me, calling upon Indra at evening and at dawn.

RV 5.32.12: For thus indeed I hear you, as you move according to the seasons and bestow riches upon the inspired singers. What do your priestly friends gain, O Indra, who have placed their desire in you?
I meditate upon the Great One, the Great and Powerful among men, for Indra, the truly powerful; for the one who is not powerful [is surpassed] by him.
He who, being praised, has observed this benevolence toward him in the contest for booty among the people in the assembly.
Thus, O Indra, being mindful of us through our hymns, you, O Bull, have fastened the yoke-halter of your bay steeds.
O Maghavan, those who thus according to your pleasure shall carry you forward—you will overcome the people.
O Indra, let not those lofty ones of ours be unyoked through lack of prayer;
mount that chariot, O wielder of the thunderbolt, for you, O God, being master of good horses, hold the reins.
O Indra, when many hymns of praise were offered to you, you fought for cattle among the pastures;
you fashioned even the name of the Dāsa in the battles for Sūrya in his own dwelling, like a bull.
O Indra, we are yours, as are these men who have been born as a host, and the chariots that have come forth.
May he whose strength is like a serpent come to us—he who is to be invoked like Bhaga at the offerings, the beloved one.
O Indra, for you have the power that is to be fulfilled, and as the immortal, you display manly deeds;
as such, O possessor of wealth, grant us brilliant riches. I praise the gift of the most bountiful one.
Thus, O Hero, protect us with your aids; favor the singers who praise you, O Indra.
And when the prize is won, be pleased with those who offer the skin [of the Soma], the sweet, well-pressed, and delightful drink.
Moreover, these gifts of the liberal Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa and lord of gold, have been bestowed upon me.
May the ten white horses of this Gairikṣita bear me hither; may we now be united through the willful acts of him who dwells on the mountain heights.
And those crimson steeds of Mārutāśva, whose gifts are according to his will, have come at the distribution of the sacrifice.
Cyavatāna, bestowing thousands upon me, has sung for the sake of beauty, like a noble man following in succession.
And those well-pleasing, radiant, and well-directed steeds of Dhvanya, the son of Lakṣmaṇya,
have come to me with the greatness of wealth, like cows entering the stall of the seer Saṃvaraṇa.
The ageless, heavenly *svadhā* follows the peerless wonder-worker according to his own nature.
Press the juice! Cook the offerings! Bestow further gifts upon him who is borne by prayer, the one praised by many.
He, the bounteous lord, has filled his belly with Soma and has rejoiced in the sweet draught;
even as he, the wielder of great weapons, directed the thousand-edged bolt for Uśanas to slay the wild beast.
RV 5.34.3.1 He who presses Soma for him, whether at the distilling-vessel or at the udder, indeed becomes radiant.

RV 5.34.3.2 The powerful Śakra drives away the evil-doer; the bountiful Maghavan, who is a friend to the wise, makes his body beautiful. RV 5.34.4.1 Whose father he has slain, whose mother, and whose brother—Śakra does not shrink from such a one.
He seeks out this man who offers what is presented; he does not shrink from the one who performs his service, for he is a source of wealth.

He does not desire to be grasped by five or ten [who are unrighteous], nor does he associate with the one who presses no Soma, even if that one is prosperous. Indeed, he overcomes him by that means or slays him, for he is a shaker; he grants a share in the cattle-filled stall to the one who seeks the gods.

Possessing powerful jaws, he strikes down the wheel in battle; he is the adversary of those who do not press the soma, the prosperer of those who do. Indra, the terrifier of all, the subduer, the Āryan, leads the Dāsa according to his will.
He gathers together the sustenance of the niggard to plunder it, and he distributes excellent wealth to the donor.
Even in a fortress, no man whatsoever can hold his ground, whoever has provoked the might of this [Indra].
When Indra, the Maghavan, brought together two wealthy clans with all their hosts for the sake of beautiful cattle, he made one of them his ally;
trembling, the Shaker released the herd of kine along with his warriors.

I praise Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, who possesses a thousand songs, O Agni—the peerless banner of the noble one. For him may the waters flow together in abundance; in him let there be powerful and brilliant dominion.
O Indra, bring forth that most effective will of yours for our protection.
For us, [grant] one who overcomes the people, a winner in battles, invincible in contests for booty. O Indra, whatever four [treasures] you have, or whatever three, O hero,
or whatever belongs to the five peoples— bring that aid well to us.
We invoke your most excellent aid, you who are most powerful.
For you were born with the impulse of a bull; O Indra, you are victorious through your manifestations. For you are a bull for the sake of bestowing bounty; your strength is that of a bull.

O Indra, your own dominion is bold, your mind is resolute, and your manly power is all-surpassing. O wielder of the stone, O Lord of a hundred powers, O Master of Might, come down with your entire chariot against that mortal who acts as an enemy.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, men who have spread the sacrificial grass invoke you— the fierce and primordial one— among the many for the winning of booty.
O Indra, [grant us] that which is invincible, that which goes at the head in battles.
Protect the chariot that speeds to every prize, seeking booty;
come to our chariot, O Indra, with your wisdom. O Most Mighty One, may we win what is desirable; may we establish glory in heaven and compose a hymn of praise in heaven.
May that Indra come, he who knows how to bestow treasures as a gift of riches. Like a thirsty bull roaming the desert, longing for water, may he drink the pressed stalk.
O Hero, Lord of Bay Steeds, let the Soma rise to your jaws and cheeks like [water] upon the back of a mountain.
O King, invoked by many, may we all rejoice in you with our songs, as one urges on swift steeds.

O wielder of the stone, invoked by many, my mind trembles like a revolving wheel through fear of my lack of devotion; would that your singer, O Maghavan, possessor of abundant wealth, might ever praise you from his chariot, O ever-prospering one!
Like a pressing-stone, this singer of yours, O Indra, raises his voice loudly as he exerts himself.

O Maghavan, bestow wealth with your left hand; O Lord of the Bay Steeds, do not be averse with your right. May the Bull Heaven increase you, the Bull; as a Bull, you are borne by your two Bulls, the Bay Steeds.
May he, the bull with the bull-chariot, the fair-jawed one of bull-like will, grant us [victory] in battle, O wielder of the thunderbolt.

May the settlements bow down before this youth Śrutaratha, offering their service, even as he, rich in prize-horses, bestowed two red, spirited steeds accompanied by three hundred [others]. May the settlements bow down before this youth Śrutaratha, offering their service, even as he, rich in prize-horses, bestowed two red, spirited steeds accompanied by three hundred [others].
May the settlements bow down before this youth Śrutaratha, offering their service, O Maruts.
He vies with the radiance of the sun, being invoked, with his back anointed with ghee, moving with ease.

For him may the unerring dawns shine forth, who says, "Let us press the Soma for Indra. With the fire kindled and the sacrificial grass strewn, the sacrificer, having yoked the pressing-stones and pressed the Soma, shall sing his praise.
RV 5.37.2: The pressing-stones of him whose vigorous voice speaks, while the Adhvaryu priest has sacrificed with the oblation across the river.
RV 5.37.3: This bride goes seeking her husband, who shall carry her away as his vigorous queen.
May his chariot be renowned for glory and let it thunder; may he bring back many thousands as his prize.
That king does not waver in whom Indra drinks the potent Soma accompanied by the cattle;
he leads forth his warriors, slays the Vṛtra, and dwells among the people, nourishing his auspicious name.
May he prosper in peace and prevail in battle; may he conquer both opposing armies when they clash.
He who has pressed the Soma and offers it to Indra shall be dear to Sūrya and dear to Agni.
O Indra, lord of a hundred powers, your gift of wealth is vast; your bounty is far-reaching.
Therefore, O ruler of all people, O lord of noble dominion, bestow upon us glorious riches.
O most powerful Indra, when you bestow that glorious nourishment which is worthy of renown,
it spreads abroad— most far-famed and difficult to surpass, O golden-hued one. O wielder of the stone,
those vital energies of yours are like abundant streams of thought.
Both gods, you rule over heaven and earth for our protection.
And so, O slayer of Vṛtra, from whatever power of yours it may be, bring us manly strength; you who take delight in manly valor, bring it to us.
Now, O Śatakratu, through these aids of yours, may we be well-protected under your shelter, O Indra; O Hero, may we be well-protected.
O Indra, whatever wonderful wealth there is that is bestowed by you, O wielder of the stone, O Adrivat—
O finder of wealth, bring us that bounty with both hands.
O Indra, bring us that which you deem most excellent and celestial. May we know this of yours, as you grant it from your boundless store.
RV 5.39.3.1–2: With that celebrated and lofty mind of yours which is intent on giving and attaining success, O wielder of the stone, burst open even the firmest [fortresses] to win us booty.
RV 5.39.4.1: [I praise] the most generous among your wealthy patrons, the king of the peoples.
To Indra for his praise, many songs have been offered with delight.
For him, this poetic word, this hymn, is to be recited for Indra.
To him, who is borne by the sacred prayer (*brahman*), the Atris magnify their songs; the Atris adorn their songs.
Come hither; drink the Soma pressed by the stones, O Lord of Soma!
O bull Indra, best slayer of Vṛtra, come with your bulls!
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull, and this pressed Soma is a bull.
O Bull Indra, O best slayer of Vṛtra, with your bulls!
As a bull, I invoke you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids.
O Bull Indra, O best slayer of Vṛtra, with your bulls!

The consumer of the dregs, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, the overcomer of the swift, the impetuous king, the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma—having yoked his two bay horses, may Indra come hither; may he exhilarate himself at the midday libation.
O Sūrya, when the Asura Svarbhānu pierced you with darkness, [Indra released you].
As one who does not know the field, like a bewildered man, they looked upon the worlds.
Then, O Indra, you struck down the magic illusions of Svarbhānu as they rolled from heaven. With the fourth sacred prayer (*brahman*), Atri found the Sun hidden by the lawless darkness.

Let not the malevolent one, harmed by malice and seized by fear, swallow me up while I am here belonging to you. You, O Mitra, are the one whose bounty is true; may you two, together with King Varuṇa, protect me.
The Brahman priest, harnessing the pressing-stones and serving them, seeks to win over the gods with his hymn and honors them with reverence.

Atri established the eye of Sūrya in heaven; he dispelled the magical illusions of Svarbhānu. Indeed, when the Asura Svarbhānu pierced the Sun with darkness, the Atris found him again, for no others were able.
Who indeed, O Mitra and Varuṇa, seeking the *ṛta*, would offer you a gift from the great heaven or from the earth?
May you protect us in the seat of *ṛta*, or grant us strengths like those who win cattle for the sacrifice.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra, Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts take pleasure in us.
RV_05.041.02.2 Or those who, with reverences, offer a well-fashioned hymn of praise to the bounteous Rudra, being in harmony with him;

RV_05.041.03.1 O Aśvins, you who are most swift to come, I shall call upon you in the flight of the wind for the prosperity of the chariot-borne one; And bring forth a prayer to the Asura of heaven, even as one brings food to a worthy sacrificer.
RV_05.041.04.1 Forward [come] the victorious ones: the divine Kaṇva, the Hotṛ, Trita from heaven, Vāta, and Agni, acting in harmony.
RV_05.041.04.2 Pūṣan, Bhaga, and all-nourishing Viśvabhojas have come forth like those with the swiftest horses to the race.
RV_05.041.05.1 Bring forward your wealth with its harnessed horses; may our prayer be established for the seeking of riches and for protection.
The Hotṛ-priest of Auśija is truly gracious through his ways, those ways of yours, O Maruts, who are swift.

Bring forth Vāyu, who yokes his chariot; bring forth the god, the inspired singer, with hymns of praise. Seeking your favor, O upholders of *ṛta*, may the wise and noble wives bestow upon us here what is good for our devotion.
I approach you with worshipful hymns of praise, with the great, illuminating songs of heaven.
Dawn and Night, like two wise women, bring all sacrifices for the mortal man.
Bestowing gifts, I sing to you, the nourishing heroes, to Vāstoṣpati and Tvaṣṭṛ.
May the blessed *dhiṣaṇā*, in harmony with our salutations, [grant] the lords of the forest and the plants for the pursuit of wealth.
May the mountains be for our protection and our offspring—those well-guided ones who are like Vasu heroes.
May the praiseworthy Āptya, the worshipful one, ever increase our hymn for us, he who is manly in his favor.

I have praised the embryo of the bull of the earth, Trita, the offspring of the waters, with a perfect hymn. Agni, like a steed with his vital strengths, is glorified; he whose hair is flame consumes the forests. How shall we speak to the great one, the son of Rudra? What shall we say to Bhaga, who is mindful of wealth?
May the waters and the plants protect us, as well as the sky, the forests, the mountains, and the tree-haired [trees].
May the Lord of Strength hear our songs—he who is more swift than the wind, the vigorous one who traverses all.
May the waters hear us, bright as cities, as they flow from the mountain that is being split open by the ladles.
We know indeed who you are, O mighty ones; we shall proclaim it, O wonder-workers, as we receive what is desirable.
Even strong birds do not descend upon the mortal whom you pursue with your weapons in your fury.
I have proclaimed the divine and earthly generations, and the waters, for the sake of the noble sacrificer.
May the heavens increase, the songs with their bright summits; may the surging waters swell forth at the pressing.
At every step, my old age has been laid down by Varūtrī, the mighty one, and by her protections.
May the great mother Rasā attend us, together with the patrons—she who is straight-handed and whose path is straight.
How may we worship with homage the bounteous Maruts, who come swiftly when they are praised? O Maruts, you of great renown, [we call] upon you when you are praised.
May Ahi Budhnya not deliver us over to harm; may he be our defender against those who attack us.
Thus indeed does the mortal win you, O gods, for the sake of offspring rich in cattle; thus does the mortal win you, O gods.
RV_05.041.17.2 May Nirṛti swallow even this old age of mine, along with the nourishment of my auspicious body.
RV_05.041.18.1 O Gods, may we obtain that benevolence of yours, strengthening food, through the praise of the cow, O Vasus.
RV_05.041.18.2 May she, the bountiful and merciful goddess, hastening toward us, come for our well-being.
May Iḷā, the mother of the herd, or Urvaśī with the rivers, favor us;
or may Urvaśī, dwelling in the great heaven, being praised, cover us with the gift of the living one.
May she attend to us for the sake of the nourishment of strength.
May this most auspicious hymn now reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga, and Aditi with our inspired thought.
May the Asura, whose path is unassailable and who brings bliss, hear us—he who is born from the mountain and is the priest of the five peoples.
May Aditi accept my hymn of praise, as a mother receives her dear and beloved son.

The sacred prayer (*brahman*) which is dear, ordained by the gods, and which brings bliss to Mitra and Varuṇa—may I [attain] that. Exalt the most wise among the sages; drench him with honey and clarified butter.
May the god Savitṛ impel for us desirable, ready, and brilliant riches.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, unite us with a favorable mind, with cattle, with wise patrons, and with well-being;
unite us with the sacred prayer ordained by the gods, and with the benevolence of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice.
The god Bhaga, Savitṛ the apportioner of wealth, and Indra, the conqueror of Vṛtra, are the winners of riches.
May Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and Purandhi—the immortal, swift ones—protect us.
Let us proclaim the deeds of the one accompanied by the Maruts, the unassailable, the victorious, and the undecaying.
O Maghavan, neither those of old, nor those of later times, nor anyone of the present has ever equaled your heroic power.

Praise Bṛhaspati, the first bestower of treasures, the winner of riches— he who, possessing abundant wealth, comes most beneficently to the one who praises and lauds him, calling upon him. Accompanied by your protections, O Bṛhaspati, the liberal patrons remain unharmed and blessed with heroic sons.
RV 5.42.8: Those who are givers of horses, or those who are givers of cattle, and those who are givers of garments—among them let there be auspicious wealth.
RV 5.42.9: Make their wealth flow away, those who enjoy while not giving to us in return for our hymns;
drive those haters of prayer far from the sun, as they grow strong in their lawless ways at the impulse [of their own will].
RV 5.42.10.1: O Maruts, strike down with wheel-less [missiles] that demon who shows himself at the feast of the gods.

5.42.10.2: He who reviles the ritual labor of one who exerts himself for you—he, though sweating, shall have his desires rendered worthless. 5.42.11.1: Praise him indeed, who has good arrows and a good bow, he who rules over every healing medicine.
Sacrifice to Rudra for great goodwill; honor the divine Asura with prostrations.

May the domestic ones who are skillful-handed, the wives of the bull, the rivers fashioned by Vibhvan, Sarasvatī, Bṛhaddivā, and Rākā—may these radiant goddesses, bestowing gifts, grant us wide space.
I offer this newest, newly-born hymn of wisdom to the Great One, the excellent refuge.
He who, fashioning forms within the womb of his daughter, brought all this into being for us.
O singer, may you now attain the Lord of the Sacrifice, who thunders and roars, with this perfect praise.
He who, possessing clouds and possessing waters, sends forth lightning, drenching both heaven and earth;
may this hymn reach the host of Maruts, the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones.
Desire calls me for wealth and well-being; praise the tireless ones whose horses are spotted deer.
May this hymn of praise reach the earth, the mid-air, the trees, and the plants for the sake of wealth.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
Bring to us wealth and heroic sons, and all immortal blessings, O Immortals.
May the cows, hastening to their goal, come to us unharmed with milk and honey.
For great wealth, the inspired singer repeatedly invokes the seven vast ones who bring bliss.
With fair praise and reverence, let him turn hither Heaven and Earth, the unerring, for the sake of strength.
May the Father and Mother, sweet of speech and skillful-handed, protect us in every battle, they who are glorious.
O Adhvaryus, having prepared the honeyed mead, bring the beautiful, bright [juice] to Vāyu.
Like a Hotṛ, drink first of this; O God, we have offered the sweet mead to you for your exhilaration.
The ten fingers, the two arms, and the two skillful hands that prepare the Soma join together the pressing-stone.
The stalk, well-hoofed and dwelling on the mountain, has yielded the bright, shimmering juice of the honeyed drink.
Soma has been pressed for you who take delight in it, for the sake of wisdom, for skill, and for great exhilaration.
O Indra, being invoked, bring your two beloved tawny steeds, well-yoked to the chariot, hitherward at the time of harnessing.

O Agni, bring hither by the god-traversed paths the great Aramati, the divine lady who is in harmony with us, who is honored with homage and offered oblations—the lofty one who knows the *ṛta*, for the exhilaration of the sweet mead.
They anoint him, as if spreading him out, like inspired singers; they heat him with fire as if he were a fatty membrane.
Like a son upon his father’s lap, the most beloved *gharma* has been set down, performing the rite for Agni.
Let the great, lofty, and most auspicious song go forth like a messenger to invoke the Aśvins.
O you who bring bliss, come hither on one chariot; come to the treasure-trove, as the linchpin reaches the nave.
I have proclaimed this hymn of praise to the mighty Pūṣan and to the swift Vāyu—
those two who, by their bounty, are the inspirers of thoughts, and who are themselves the givers of wealth and booty.
O Jātavedas, being invoked, bring hither all the Maruts with their names and their forms.
Come all you Maruts to the sacrifice, to the songs and the beautiful hymn of the singer, with all your aids!
From the high heaven, from the mountain, let the worshipful Sarasvatī come to our sacrifice;
may the goddess, delighting in our call, dripping with clarity, desiring us, hear our effective speech.
Seat in his dwelling Bṛhaspati, the ordainer, blue-backed and vast. May we honor him who shines within the home, seated in his proper place—the golden-hued, ruddy one.
May the sustainer from the lofty heaven, bestowing gifts and invoked by all our hymns, come hither.

Clothed in the wives [the plants], the unerring bull, three-horned and bestower of vigor, has come. To the highest station of the Mother, to the bright place of Āyu, the praisers and the eloquent ones have gone.
With reverence, offering oblations, they purify the child for his auspicious dwelling, as men cleanse [a garment] for clothing.
Great vital strength is yours, O Agni, the great one; through our prayer, the paired [husband and wife] attend upon you, who grow old in wisdom.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in her ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious fortunes.
As of old, as of former times, as of all time, and as now, [we praise] him who sits upon the sacrificial grass, the finder of heaven, the most exalted one.
Through my song, may I milk from thee the western enclosure, the swift one who conquers, in whom thou growest strong.
For the sake of glory, those [rays] of the lower heaven are beautiful to behold; shining brightly, thou dost not urge on the quarters of the sky.
Thou art a good guardian, O wise one, not to be deceived; beyond all deceits, thy name is established in the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
The oblation follows the steed; may he, whose path is unharmed, be our companion and bestower of wealth, the Hotar-priest who brings strength.
The bull, the vigorous youth, having spread himself along the sacrificial grass, stands ageless between the two world-halves that have been established.
These well-yoked ones go forth on their course for the sacrifice, moving downward toward him, the twin sisters who increase the Holy Order.
With well-guided reins and all-controlling bits, Krivi steals away their names on the slope.
Seizing with his teeth, he shakes the tree; grasping the pressed juice, he reveals the bird within the pregnant thoughts, sounding well.
O singer of straight hymns, you shine amidst the calls for the streams; increase, O living one, toward your wives at the sacrifice.
Just as he was seen, so is he described; they have established him with his effective radiance within the waters.
Grant us great, wide space and vast dominion—mighty, heroic strength that is unshakable.
Whether he is unmarried or having wives, Sūrya, the sage, goes beyond his rivals with a mind intent on battle.
May he who possesses excellent wealth grant us protection, guarding our home from all sides against the scorcher.
By the signal of this striving one, he moves toward the preeminent Lord of Seers among those [waters] wherein is your name.
Whosoever has established him in such a state through his work, he who carries it himself shall make it successful.

The foremost of these has descended into the ocean; the libation in which they are extended does not fail. Here our heart trembles at the call of the one who impels, where the hymn exists that is bound to the purified [Soma]. For he, by the thoughts of Manasa Kṣatra, is the companion of Evāvada, the worshipful and the seated.

RV_05.044.10.2 With the exhilarating draughts of Avatsāra, may we win the most powerful prize, which is to be attained even by the wise. RV_05.044.11.1 The falcon is their Aditi; the exhilaration of Viśvavāra, of the worshipful and artful one, is like a girth. RV_05.044.11.2 They strive together to go toward one after another; they know the horn and the drinking-place that surrounds them.
Sadāpṛṇa, the sacrificer, shall strike down our enemies; Bāhuvṛkta, Śrutavid, and Tarya are with you.
He goes toward both boons and shines when he joins his troop with those who are well-disposed to depart.
Sutambhara, the lord of the virtuous, the sacrificer’s protector, is the one who draws forth the udder of all prayers.
Bringing the cows, he has drawn forth the flavorful milk; the one who recites masters it, not the one who sleeps. The *ṛc*s desire him who is awake; to him who is awake, the *sāmans* go.
To him who is awake, this Soma says: "I am yours, at home in your friendship."
Agni is awake; the *ṛc*s desire him. Agni is awake; to him the *sāmans* go.

Agni is awake; to him this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship. Finding the light of heaven, they have opened the rock with hymns; the singers have come for the approaching dawn.
The enclosure-gates were thrown open; the Sun ascended to heaven; O God, you have opened the doors for mankind.
Like splendor dispelling darkness, Sūrya has come forth; the Mother of the Cows, knowing her way, has gone out from the wide space.
The rivers flow with desert-like waters, their waves a source of refreshment; like a well-set pillar, the sky is firmly established.
For this hymn, the child of the mountain [has been born] for the sake of the ancient birth of the great ones.
The mountain has opened wide; heaven has been perfected. Seeking to win them over, they have subdued the earth.
With well-spoken words, with speech beloved by the gods, I shall now invoke Indra and Agni for protection.
For indeed, with hymns and well-performed sacrifices, the seers, seeking to win them over, worship the Maruts.
Come now today; let us be of good intent, and let us drive away misfortune to a wider distance. Let us keep hostilities far away and at a distance; let us go forward toward the sacrificer.
O friends, let us perform this prayer by which one opens the mother’s stall for the cattle,
that prayer by which Manu conquered Viśiśipra, and by which the merchant Vaṅku obtained the water-filled place.
Here the pressing-stone, guided by hands, has roared— the stone with which the Navagvas sang praise for ten months.

Seeking the *ṛta*, Saramā found the cows; Aṅgiras made all things true. When at the dawning of this magnificent goddess, the Aṅgirases sang together with the cattle, their source was in the highest dwelling-place; by the path of *ṛta*, Saramā found the cows.
May Sūrya come with his seven horses to the field that extends over his wide path; may the swift falcon fly toward the soma-juice; may the youthful sage shine as he goes among the cattle.
Sūrya has ascended the bright ocean when he has yoked his tawny, straight-backed steeds.
As with water they guided the ship, the wise ones; the waters, listening, stood still nearby.
I place within the waters your prayer that wins the light, by which the Navagvas crossed over the ten months.
Through this prayer may we have the gods as our guardians; through this prayer may we pass beyond distress.

Like a wise horse, I have yoked myself to the pole; I bear that which carries across, seeking aid. I do not desire its unyoking nor its turning back again; may the wise leader lead me straight upon the path.
O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and gods, grant us strength, O Maruts and Viṣṇu!
May both the Nāsatyas, Rudra, the divine dames (gnās), Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Sarasvatī take pleasure [in this].
I invoke Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sun, the Earth, the Sky, the Maruts, and the Mountains;
I call upon Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, Śaṃsa, and Savitṛ for our protection.
May Viṣṇu and Vāta, the infallible givers of wealth, and Soma grant us joy;
may the Ṛbhus and the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ and Vibhvan, likewise grant us riches.
And may that divine host of Maruts come to us, dwelling in heaven, the holy ones, to sit upon the sacred grass.
May Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan grant us protection, and may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman provide us with a secure refuge.
And may those mountains, worthy of praise, and the brightly shining rivers be our protectors in our distress.
May Bhaga, the distributor, come with power and aid; may the far-reaching Aditi hear my invocation.

May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us for the sake of progeny and the winning of spoil. Those who belong to the earth and those who abide in the domain of the waters—may those goddesses, who are easily invoked, grant us protection.
And may the divine consorts go forth: Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī, and Rāṭ.
May Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; may the goddesses come at the appointed time of women.
Setting forth, she goes from heaven, speaking as the great mother awakening her daughter. Seeking to win favor, the youthful maiden, inspired thought, calls aloud to the fathers at their seat.
Swift, hastening toward those waters, they have taken their stand at the navel of immortality.
Endless and wide, their paths go all around heaven and earth on every side.
The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one, the fair-winged bird, has entered the womb of the ancient father.
Placed in the midst of heaven, the dappled stone has stepped forth; it guards the two ends of the mid-air.
Four bear him up, providing security, while ten suckle the embryo so that he may move. His three-layered cows, most excellent, traverse the ends of heaven in an instant.
O people, this beautiful form with its secret name is that which men practice, wherein the rivers stand still and the waters flow.
Since two others, born here and there, support him—the twin brothers who share the same kinship with their mother.
For him they extend their prayers and their works; like mothers weaving garments for their son, they weave for him.
Rejoicing at the sprinkling, the bulls go toward the brides along the path of heaven.
May this be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may this be so, O Agni. May this be for us health and well-being; may this recitation be auspicious.
May we attain a firm footing and a secure foundation. Homage to the great Heaven, the dwelling place!
When shall we meditate upon our own dear abode, great with its own dominion and its own glory?
When the crafty one, choosing the waters, spreads them out across the cloud in the unfailing mid-air?
They have stretched out the path that nourishes heroes, through the entire mid-air with their uniform course.
The god-seeking man drives away the waters to the west and the farther ones; with the waters of the east, he advances further.
With the pressing-stones day after day, through the nights, he hurls the most excellent thunderbolt at the wielder of magic.
He who, even as he moves about in his own dwelling, brings together a hundred days or lets them pass.
I have beheld his course like that of an axe; I have seen the face of this beautiful form for my enjoyment.

When he bestows treasure upon the people who call upon him for aid, it is as if he were providing a dwelling full of food. He, the four-faced one, exerts himself with his tongue, wearing lovely garments, as Varuṇa strives to restrain the enemy.
We do not know his true nature as a man, from whom Bhaga and Savitṛ bestow desirable wealth. I seek today for you the god Savitṛ and Bhaga, who distributes the treasure of mankind.
O Aśvins, heroes who enjoy many things, may I turn you both hither day after day, seeking your friendship.
Knowing the departure of the Asura, worship the god Savitṛ with hymns. Let him who understands speak to him with reverence—the one who distributes the highest treasure to mankind.
Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Aditi bestow desirable gifts ungrudgingly; they clothe themselves in the light of dawn.
Indra, Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the wondrous ones—have brought forth auspicious days. May the invincible Savitṛ grant us that protection; may the life-giving rivers follow after it.
When I, the priest of the sacrifice, speak these words, may we become masters of wealth, rich in booty.

RV_05.049.05.1 Those who offer such homage to the Vasus, and those who address Mitra and Varuṇa with hymns of praise— RV_05.049.05.2 May the monster depart; make wide room for us! Through the protection of Heaven and Earth, may we rejoice. RV_05.050.01.1 Let every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader.
Everyone strives for wealth; let him choose glory that he may prosper.
O God, O Leader, those who are yours and those who follow this instruction—may we, through you, be united with wealth and with the one worthy of praise, for you are our companion.
Therefore, honor our guests; therefore, show hospitality to our wives.
May the Expeller drive far away every enemy who stands in our path.
Where the bearer has been set down, the beast of the trough has run forth.
Manly-minded, with heroes in his home, he wins the floods like a wise sage.
O God, this chariot-lord of yours is a leader; he is wealth, a blessing.
