For wealth, for well-being, we meditate upon him who praises the food; we meditate upon him who praises the God.
O Agni, come with all your helpers for the drinking of the pressed juice; come with the gods for the offering of the oblation.
O you whose thoughts are fixed on the *Ṛta*, come to the sacrifice, you whose laws are true.
Drink with the tongue of Agni.
O wise one, come with the sages, O truthful one, with those who travel at dawn,
together with the gods, for the drinking of Soma.
This Soma, pressed in the mortar, is poured into the vessel for Indra and Vāyu, as their beloved draught.
O Vāyu, come hither to enjoy it, being pleased by the offering of the oblation.
Drink of the pressed juice for the sake of refreshment!
O Indra and Vāyu, you two deserve the drinking of these pressed juices;
may you both enjoy them, being stainless, for the sake of refreshment.
The Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra and Vāyu;
like rivers flowing downward, they go toward the offering.
In harmony with all the gods, with the Aśvins, and with Uṣas, [may he come].

Come, O Agni, and rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri! In harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa, in harmony with Soma and Viṣṇu, come, O Agni, and rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri!
In harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus, in harmony with Indra and Vāyu, come hither, O Agni; rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri.
May the Aśvins and Bhaga grant us well-being; may the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, grant us well-being.
May Pūṣan, the Asura, grant us well-being; may Heaven and Earth grant us well-being with their benevolent thought.

For the sake of well-being, let us invoke Vāyu and Soma, who is the lord of the world for the sake of well-being. For the sake of well-being, [we invoke] Bṛhaspati with his entire host; may the Ādityas be for our well-being.
May all the gods today grant us well-being; may Agni Vaiśvānara, the Vasu, grant us well-being.
May the divine Ṛbhus protect us for our well-being; may Rudra preserve us from distress.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, grant us well-being; O wealthy Pathyā, grant us well-being.
May Indra and Agni grant us well-being; O Aditi, grant us well-being.
May we follow the path with well-being, like the sun and the moon.
May we come together again with one who gives, who does not strike, and who knows.
O Śyāvāśva, sing boldly with the Maruts who are accompanied by hymns—
those worshipful ones who, according to their wont, rejoice in guileless glory.
For they are indeed the companions of steadfast power, bold in their daring.
On their journey, those bold ones protect all beings by their own power.
Like rushing bulls, they leap over the nights.
And thus we celebrate the greatness of the Maruts in heaven and on earth.
Upon the Maruts let us boldly place our hymn and sacrifice—
those who, throughout all human generations, protect mortal man from harm;
those worthy ones, the bounteous givers, heroes of unimpaired strength.
I shall praise the sacrifice for the Maruts, the worshipful ones of heaven.
The lofty heroes have come with their golden ornaments and weapons; they have hurled forth their spears.
Following these Maruts, who are like laughing lightnings, the radiance has risen of its own accord from heaven.
Those who have grown strong on earth, those who are in the wide mid-air,
or in the gathering place of the rivers, or in the assembly of the great heaven—
praise the host of Maruts, truly powerful and skillful.
And indeed, for your glory, those swift men have themselves yoked their horses.
And indeed, on the Paruṣṇī river, the pure ones have clothed themselves in wool.
And with the tires of their chariots, they shatter the mountain by their might.
The paths that come from afar, the divergent paths, the paths within, and the following paths—by these names for me, they offer the sacrifice as a wide-spreading expanse.
Then the men offer it down; then the teams of horses offer it down.
Then, like those from afar, they displayed wondrous forms to be beheld.
Chanting hymns and seeking water, the singers danced toward the spring.
Some of them were like thieves to me, yet they became helpers for my sight and brilliance.
Those who are lofty, whose spears are like lightning, who are seers and wise ordainers—
to that host of Maruts, O seer, pay homage and delight them with your song.
Come, O seer, toward the host of Maruts, as a woman approaches her friend with gifts.

Or from heaven, O bold ones, impelled by our prayers through your might, hasten hither. Now, mindful of them, let not the vessels of these gods fail us; may he be united with the liberal patrons who are renowned for their journeys and adorned with ornaments.

RV 5.52.16.1: Those wise patrons who, in their desire for kinship, have declared for me the cow; they have declared *Pṛśni* to be the mother. RV 5.52.16.2: And so, the skillful ones have declared the father to be the impetuous *Rudra*. RV 5.52.17.1: Seven times seven powerful ones have each given me a hundred.
RV 5.52.17.2: Upon the Yamunā, I have cleansed the famous gift of cattle; I have cleansed the gift of horses.
RV 5.53.1.1: Who knows their birth? Or who was formerly in the favor of the Maruts? RV 5.53.1.2: When they, the tireless ones, have harnessed their steeds.
Who has heard of those who stood upon their chariots, and how they went? To which liberal patron did the allied rains flow together with the *īḷā* offerings?
They have told this to me—those who came hither through the heavens with their winged steeds in the exhilaration of the soma.
"O men, O youths, blameless ones, look upon these and praise them!"—
those who possess their own splendor in their ointments, in their axes, in their garlands, in their golden ornaments,
in their rings, on their chariots, and in their bows.
O Maruts, givers of quickening rain, I set my heart upon your chariots for joy,
like the heavens moving with showers of rain.
The men of liberal bounty have shaken down the treasure-chest of heaven for the one who offers oblations.
They release Parjanya throughout the two worlds; the rains flow across the desert wastes.
Having burst their banks with their surge, the rivers have rushed forth through the mid-air like milch-cows, like swift horses at the unyoking of their paths as they spread abroad.
Come hither, O Maruts, from heaven, from the intermediate region, and from the earth; do not stay away from us from the far distance.
Let not the Rasā, the Anitabhā, the Kubhā, or the Krumu, nor the Sindhu river, detain you.
May the Sarayu river, rich in its waters, not stand in your way; may your favor be with us.
The rain-showers follow that host of yours, the brilliant Marut-host of chariots, the troop of the ever-youthful ones.
We would follow after every one of their hosts, every troop, and every company with fair praises and with our prayers.
To which noble-born one, to whom offerings have been presented, have they gone forth today?
O Maruts,
with this course by which you bring undecaying seed-grain for our children and progeny— grant us that bounty for which we pray to you, and all-encompassing prosperity.
May we pass beyond reproach through blessings, leaving behind blame and hostilities.
Having rained down health, well-being, and healing waters upon us at dawn, O Maruts, may we be with you.
That mortal man, O heroes Maruts, shall be truly blessed with gods and truly blessed with heroic sons.
May we be those whom you protect.
Praise the liberal patrons; may they take delight in the course of this singer like cattle in a pasture.
Summon them with song like old friends, and celebrate those who desire [you].
I have fashioned this speech for the Marut host, self-luminous and shakers of the mountains.
Sing forth a great hymn of manly valor to those who praise the *gharma* oblation, who sacrifice upon the back of heaven, and whose glory is radiant.
O Maruts, your powerful, water-seeking, life-increasing, horse-yoked, and far-reaching [teams] advance.
They hold together with lightning; Trita roars; the waters sound as they flow around the woods.

The Maruts—men of lightning-splendor, who strike with stones, whose flash is like the wind, shakers of mountains; though they are accompanied by the clouds, they are for a moment covered in hail, roaring with thunder, impetuous, and of exalted might.
O Rudras, you who are skillful and shakers of all, you traverse the nights, the days, the mid-air, and the regions.
When you drive across the plains like ships upon the sea, O Maruts, you pass through difficult places and suffer no harm.
That heroic power of yours, O Maruts, and that greatness of yours has extended far, like the sun extending its course.
Like these [mares] on their course, whose splendor is ungraspable, when you went down to the mountain against her who gave no horse;
O wise Maruts, your host shone forth as you stripped the tree like a moth.
Now, being of one mind, lead our devotion along an easy path, even as the eye leads him who walks.
RV_05.054.07.1 He is not conquered, O Maruts; he is not slain; he does not fail; he does not tremble; he does not come to harm.
RV_05.054.07.2 Neither his wealth nor his aids fail him—whichever seer or king you bring to perfection.
RV_05.054.08.1 Like men who possess teams of horses and conquer hosts, like Aryaman, the Maruts are bearers of water-skins.
RV_05.054.08.2 When the impetuous ones have roared, they cause the spring to swell; they drench the earth with the juice of honey.
RV_05.054.09.1 This earth becomes sloping for the Maruts, and the sky becomes sloping for them as they advance.
RV_05.054.09.2 Sloping are the paths through the mid-air; sloping are the mountains that grant quickening gifts.
O Maruts, you who bear the spoils together, heroes of heaven, when the sun has risen, you rejoice, O men of the sky.
Your horses do not falter as they gallop; instantly you reach the end of this journey.
Spears are upon your shoulders, anklets on your feet, golden ornaments on your chests, O Maruts, and splendor upon your chariot.
The flames of fire are in his two arms, the lightnings; golden helmets are spread upon his heads.
O Maruts, you shake that firmament of ungraspable splendor, its bright fruit.
When they flash forth, their enclosures close together; the seekers of Truth raise a far-reaching shout.
O wise Maruts, may we be charioteers of the wealth you bestow, which is full of vitality.
O Maruts, grant us that thousandfold bounty which does not fail, like *Tiṣya* from heaven.
O Maruts, you favor the man of desirable heroes with wealth; you favor the seer who is inspired by the *Sāman*.
You bestow a swift steed as prize upon the Bharata; you grant a king who is prompt to hear.

I beg of you that wealth, O you who are swift to help, by which we may extend ourselves over men like the sun. O Maruts, graciously accept this word of mine, by whose power we may cross over a hundred winters.
The Maruts, ever eager for sacrifice, with gleaming spears and golden discs upon their breasts, have assumed great vigor.
They hasten along with swift, well-governed horses; as they go forth in splendor, their chariots follow. You yourselves have acquired strength as you know how; O great ones, you rule far and wide.
And they have measured out the mid-air with their might; as they go toward splendor, their chariots have rolled forth.

Born together, well-being-bringers, grown together, these heroes have increased further for the sake of glory. Radiant like the rays of the sun, as they go toward splendor, their chariots have rolled forth.

O Maruts, your greatness is worthy of adoration; it is worthy of being beheld, like the very sight of the sun. Furthermore, establish us in immortality. As they went forth in splendor, their chariots followed.
O Maruts, you raise up the rain from the ocean; you, the possessors of abundance, cause the rain to fall.
O wonder-workers, your milch-cows never fail; as you go forth to glory, your chariots have rolled onward.
When you have yoked the spotted mares to the poles of the horses, you have cast off your golden mantles.
O Maruts, you scatter all rivals; as you go forth to glory, your chariots have rolled onward.

Neither mountains nor rivers can obstruct you where you have resolved to go; thither you must come, O Maruts. And even heaven and earth cannot contain you when you set out on your journey; your chariots have rolled forth to follow your splendor.
O Maruts, whatever is ancient and whatever is new, whatever is spoken, O Vasus, and whatever is recited—[all these are yours].
Be aware of all that [is yours]; the chariots have turned to follow those who go toward splendor.
O Maruts, have mercy on us; do not strike us down! Extend to us manifold protection.
Remember our hymn of praise and our friendship; the chariots have turned to follow those who go toward splendor.
O Maruts, being praised, lead us toward greater prosperity and out from our distresses;
O worshipful ones, enjoy our offering of oblations, and may we be masters of riches.
O Agni, [lead] the bold host, adorned with golden ornaments and decorations.
Today I call upon the host of Maruts from even the luminous realm of heaven.
Just as you think in your heart, so have my prayers reached you. Strengthen those who have come most closely to your invocations—those of terrible aspect.
Like a bountiful woman, the earth, struck down, comes toward us exulting. O Maruts, your impetuous force is like a fierce bear, terrible as a wild bull.
They who by their might scatter [the enemy] at will, like bulls difficult to restrain.

They cause even the heavenly stone, the mountain, the rock, to tremble with their marches. Arise now with the hymns of these who have been sprinkled together; I call upon the most abundant and unprecedented host of Maruts, like a release of cattle.
Yoke the two ruddy mares to the chariot; yoke the two red horses to the chariots.
Yoke the two swift bay steeds to the pole to draw, the best at drawing to the pole.
And let this vigorous, ruddy, loud-sounding steed be stationed here, beautiful to behold.
O Maruts, let him not delay you on your journeys; urge him forward upon your chariots.
We now invoke the Marut-host’s chariot, which seeks renown—the chariot upon which Rodasī stands together with the Maruts, bringing forth delightful treasures.
I invoke that host of yours, brilliant on its chariot, impetuous, and worthy of praise—
the host in which the well-born, fortunate, and bountiful goddess exalts herself together with the Maruts.
O Rudras, accompanied by Indra, being of one mind and mounted on golden chariots, come for our prosperity.
This thought of ours is offered to you in welcome, like a spring from heaven to one who thirsts for water.
Armed with axes and spears, wise, with good bows, arrows, and quivers;
O Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, you possess fine horses and excellent chariots—come forth with your noble weapons for glory!
You shake the sky and the mountains for the sake of the donor’s wealth; the forests bow down before you in fear as you travel.
O sons of Pṛśni, you stir up the earth when you, the fierce ones, have yoked your spotted deer for glory.
The Maruts, flashing like the wind, clothed in rain, are as perfectly alike as twins and beautifully adorned.
With tawny horses and ruddy horses, they are stainless, exceedingly swift, and as vast in their greatness as the sky.
Abounding in drops, adorned with ornaments, bounteous givers, they are brilliant to behold and possess wealth that never fails.
Well-born by birth, with golden plates upon their breasts, these singers of heaven have attained the name of immortality.
Spears are upon your shoulders, O Maruts; together with you, power is placed in your arms and strength in your hands.
Valor is in your heads, weapons upon your chariots, and every splendor is adorned upon your bodies.
O Maruts, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, chariots, and brave sons—splendid bounty indeed!
O sons of Rudra, grant us renown; may I enjoy your divine protection. Come, O heroes, O Maruts, be gracious to us—you who possess abundant wealth, are immortal, and know the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
You are hearers of truth, sages, youthful, dwelling upon the great mountains, and swelling with great power.
Now indeed I praise that powerful host of these most recent Maruts,
who drive with swift horses like storming winds and who, as self-ruling lords, exercise sovereignty over immortality.
I praise the brilliant host, the mighty one, with rings upon their hands, whose law is to shake all things, who is full of wondrous power and bestows abundant wealth.
O sage, do thou praise those men who bring delight, who are immeasurable in their greatness, and who bestow abundant wealth.
May your water-bearing steeds come hither today—those Maruts who all together impel the rain.
O Maruts, this Agni has been kindled; take pleasure in him, O youthful sages.
O worshipful ones, you bring forth for the people a vigorous king, fashioned by Vibhvan.
From you comes the club-fighter urged by his arms; from you, O Maruts, comes he who possesses good horses and noble heroes.
Like spokes, none among them is last; like days, they are born on and on, never failing in their greatness.
The sons of Pṛśni, the most excellent and most powerful, the Maruts, have united with their own thought.
When you have set forth with your spotted deer as horses, O Maruts, on chariots with strong fellies— the waters surge, the forests give way; let the bull of heaven, the sun, roar down.

Even the earth has spread wide at their coming; they have established their own power like a husband bearing his seed. For they have yoked the winds as horses to the pole, and the sons of Rudra have turned their sweat into rain.
O heroes, O Maruts, you who are rich in wealth, immortal, and knowers of the *ṛta*, have mercy upon us!
The poets, hearers of truth, youthful, with lofty songs, waxing great.
They have stirred themselves for you to grant prosperity; sing praise to Heaven! I offer the sacred law (*ṛta*) to Earth.
They sprinkle their horses, they hasten across the mid-air; they loosen their own splendor with surging waves.
The earth trembles from fear of them; like a full ship, she quivers as she moves along.
Those heroes, visible from afar, who manifest themselves with their marches, have exerted themselves within the great assembly.
Like the preeminent horn of bulls for the sake of splendor, they are like the eye of Sūrya at the unfolding of the firmament.
Like well-formed, beautiful horses, you are lovely; like young men, O heroes, you take thought for glory.
Who could reach the greatness of you, the great ones? Who, O Maruts, could attain your poetic wisdom or your manly deeds?
You indeed cause the earth to tremble as if by a scattering of dust, when you bring forth [your power] to grant us prosperity.
Like ruddy horses of the same kin, like heroes eager for combat, they have indeed fought forward.
Like well-grown youths, these men have increased; with their rains, they diminish the eye of the sun.
They, neither eldest nor youngest, but none the least, bursting forth from the depths, have grown great by their majesty.
Well-born by birth, sons of Pṛśni, heroes of heaven, come hither toward us!
Like birds that fly in rows with might from the ridges of the high heaven,
their horses— both kinds, as they know— have set the springs of the mountain flowing.
May Dyaus Aditi low for our enjoyment; may the Dawns, wonderful in their gifts, strive together for us.
These Maruts of Rudra, being praised, O seer, have caused the celestial cask to pour forth.
I praise Agni, the one of good protection, with prostrations; seated here, may he discern our prepared offering.
Like those seeking booty with their chariots, I offer my praise; may I successfully accomplish this hymn of the Maruts, turning it to the right.

The Rudras, the Maruts, who have mounted upon their famous spotted deer and upon their easy-gliding chariots—out of fear of you, O fierce ones, even the forests bow down; even the earth trembles, and even the mountain shakes.
Even the mountain, though greatly grown, was afraid; even the ridge of heaven trembled at your roar, O Maruts, when you play armed with spears and rush together like waters.
Like wealthy suitors, they have adorned their bodies with gold and their own inherent powers.
For the sake of glory, the most excellent and powerful ones have fully established their greatness upon their chariots and within their own bodies.
Among them, none is eldest and none is youngest; these brothers have grown together for the sake of prosperity.
Their father is the youthful Rudra, the skillful artisan; Pṛśni, the well-yielding cow, provides fair days for the Maruts.
Whether you, O Maruts, are in the highest, the middle, or even the lowest heaven,
O blessed ones— From there, O Rudras, and you too, O Agni, take note of this oblation which we sacrifice.
And when, O all-knowing Maruts, you and Agni carry [the offerings] from the highest ridge of heaven upon your backs.
Rejoicing, O shakers of the earth, destroyers of enemies, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the Soma.
O Agni, with the Maruts—those radiant, hymn-singing, troop-glorious ones—drink the Soma, rejoicing.
O Vaiśvānara, together with the purifying, all-pervading, life-sustaining ones, and with your ancient banner, be united.
Who are you, O heroes, most excellent ones, who have come one by one from the furthest distance? Where are your horses, where are your reins; how did you succeed, and how did you come?
On their backs is the seat; the yoke is on their nostrils.
At their haunches is the goad. These heroes have spread their thighs apart like women for the procreation of sons.
Go forth, O heroes, O young men of auspicious lineage,
so that you may be heated by fire.
May he win cattle consisting of horses, and cattle consisting of kine, numbering a hundred sheep.
The arm which Śyāvāśva, when praised, extended for his heroic patron—
And even a woman becomes more frequent, more excellent than a man who is godless and ungenerous.
She who distinguishes the exhausted, the thirsty, and the desiring one,
turns her mind toward the gods. And yet,
there is some miserly man whom they call a "non-praiser," a trafficker.
He is equal in the distribution of the prize of victory.
And the young woman, having been exhilarated, cleared a path for Śyāva;
the two ruddy steeds drew [the chariot] for Purumīḷha, the inspired sage of far-reaching fame.
He who, like Vaidadaśvi, gave me a hundred cows, bestowing them with great generosity like Taranta;
he who carries [the gods] on swift steeds, drinking the intoxicating honey-sweetness.
In this [sacrifice], they have established glories—
those whose splendor, upon their chariots, outshines both heaven and earth, like a golden ornament high in the sky.
That youthful host of Maruts, with its brilliant chariot, is blameless; it moves toward splendor, irresistible. Who now truly knows where these shakers revel?
Born of Truth, stainless, you who are full of praise,
O mortals, are leaders through this very prayer; you are hearers at the invocations of the journey.
O you who destroy the foe, may you, the worshipful ones, turn toward us those desirable riches that are manifold and radiant.
O Urmyā, carry this hymn of mine away to Dārbhya.
O Goddess, my songs are like a charioteer; And let her say this to me when the soma is pressed, at the prize-winning chariot-race:
"My desire does not turn away."
This Maghavan dwells among the cattle-rich [regions], Rathavīti, taking refuge in the mountains.
By the Eternal Law, the eternal Law is firmly established for you both, where they unyoke the horses of the Sun.
Ten hundred stood together; I beheld that one most excellent form among the gods.
O Mitra and Varuna, that is truly your greatness: those who stood still have been milked by the days.
You cause all the milch-cows of the stall to swell; for you, the single wheel has rolled forward.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, kings by your majesty, you have supported the earth and the sky.
Increase the plants and cause the cows to swell; release the rain, O ye of quickening gifts.
May your well-yoked horses carry you hither; may they come toward us with their reins held tight.

The cleansing of the clarified butter follows you; from of old, the rivers flow toward you. Increasing the renowned and wide-reaching splendor, you guard it as if with a sacrificial prayer upon the sacred grass. Reverent and firm in will, you two sit upon the throne—Mitra and Varuṇa—within the waters of Iḍā.

With hands that do not shed blood, you protect the one who performs good deeds; whomsoever you two, O Varuṇa and Mitra, shelter within your laws, O Kings, you maintain his unassailable dominion together, supported by a thousand pillars.
Clad in golden splendor, its pillar is of iron; it shines forth like a whip for a divine horse.
In the auspicious field, or in Tilvila, may we win the honey from the wagon-seat.
At the dawning of the Dawn, at the rising of the Sun, you two ascend the golden-colored seat with its bronze pillars, O Varuṇa and Mitra. From there, you two behold both Aditi and Diti.

O bounteous guardians of the world, that which is most expansive, impenetrable, and flawless protection—thereby, O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect us; may we, seeking to win, be victorious. O guardians of the *ṛta*, you whose laws are true, you mount your chariot in the highest heaven.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, for whomsoever you two protect here, for him the rain of heaven pours forth sweetness.
As sovereign rulers, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you rule over this world, beholding the light at the assembly.
We pray for your gift of rain and immortality; the thunderers move across heaven and earth.

Sovereign kings, fierce bulls, lords of heaven and earth, Mitra and Varuṇa, you who observe all people— With wondrous clouds you attend to the roar; by the magic power of the Asura, you cause the sky to rain.
Your magic power, O Mitra and Varuṇa, is established in heaven; the Sun moves as a light, a wondrous weapon.
You conceal him with cloud and rain in the sky; O Parjanya, honeyed drops surge forth.

The Maruts yoke their easy chariot for glory, like a hero in the search for cattle, O Mitra and Varuṇa. The brilliant thunders traverse the regions of the air; O sovereign kings, sprinkle us with the milk of heaven.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, Parjanya speaks forth the wondrous, brilliant, and powerful speech, rich in nourishment.
The Maruts clothe themselves in clouds through their great creative power; cause the ruddy, stainless heaven to rain.
By the law, O wise Mitra and Varuṇa, you guard the sacred ordinances through the creative power of the Asura.
By the *ṛta* you rule over the entire world; you place the sun in heaven as a wondrous chariot.
We invoke with a hymn Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies, and Mitra for you.
Having gone forth from the enclosure with your arms, you have reached the sun.
Stretch forth those two arms with benevolence toward us who sing your praise;
for your auspicious and enduring friendship is celebrated throughout all lands.
May I now attain that goal and travel upon the path of Mitra.
In the protection of this beloved one, who does no harm, they have taken refuge.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we offer you a hymn worthy of praise through our verse, so that there may be emulation among the wealthy patrons and the singers in their dwellings.
May Mitra with his fair splendors and Varuṇa come to our gathering place, to their own dwelling, for the increase of the wealthy patrons and of their friends.
O Varuṇa, you two uphold among us that great sovereign power.
Make wide room for us to win booty, for wealth, and for well-being.
While the dawn shines forth under the divine dominion, O worshipful ones, among the radiant cattle—
run hither with your feet like men carrying the pressed Soma in their hands, bearing Arcanānas.
He who has perceived [this] is of skillful intellect; let him speak for us among the gods—Varuṇa, whose songs the beautiful Mitra also accepts.
For they two are kings of most excellent luster, of far-reaching fame.
They are the lords of the good, the increasers of *ṛta*, the observers of *ṛta* among every people.
Approaching you both for protection, I invoke you first together with my companions; may we, possessing fine horses, through your wisdom, prevail in the winning of spoils.
Mitra wins a wide path even from distress for his dwelling;
for the favor of Mitra, who overcomes all, belongs to him who serves him. May we abide in the most extensive protection of Mitra.
Your aids are unassailable; they truly possess the abundance of Varuṇa.
You two, O Mitra, urge this people forward and lead them together.
Do not overlook the generous patrons, nor us, the seers; protect us in your guardianship.
O mortal, take note of the two gods of noble will who destroy the foe;
let him offer worship to Varuṇa, whose form is truth, for great joy.
For they have attained an unassailable dominion and perfect divine power.
Then, as if by a sacred law, the human race has established the sun-like light,
beautiful to behold. In this pursuit of yours, we think of the wide pasture for these chariots, and of the excellent praise of Rātahavya, with firm hymns of praise.
For then, O wondrous ones, you two [reveal] the poetic insights through the fortresses of Dakṣa; by your signal, O you of purified skill, you are perceived among the people.
That is the lofty cosmic order (*ṛta*), O Earth, which the seers desire for their renown.
Flowing forth in their courses, they stream across the broad earth like two swift-moving steeds.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who possess far-reaching vision, may we and our wise patrons come before you.
May we strive for your sovereign dominion, which is most expansive and provides abundant protection.
Truly, O Ādityas, you have attained here, O Gods, the established, lofty, and holy domain—
O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, you have attained the most exalted sovereignty.
When you two, O Varuṇa and Mitra, sit upon your golden seat.
O supporters of the peoples, destroyers of enemies, grant us happiness as you approach.
For all the gods who possess all knowledge—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—follow their sacred laws like footsteps; they protect the mortal from harm.
For they are true, touching the cosmic order (*ṛta*), upholders of *ṛta* among every people; they are excellent leaders, bounteous givers, who create wide space even from distress.
Who indeed among you—O Mitra or Varuṇa—is not praised for his own persons?
RV 5.67.5: That prayer of yours we urge forward; from the Atris it urges itself forward. RV 5.68.1:
Sing forth with inspired song to Mitra and Varuṇa. RV 5.68.2: They whose dominion is great uphold the lofty Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
The two sovereign kings who have ghee as their source, both Mitra and Varuṇa,
the gods praised among the gods— may they two enable us to obtain great earthly and celestial wealth.
Great is your dominion among the gods;
they honor the *ṛta* with *ṛta*, and they have attained impetuous skill.
The two guileless gods increase in strength.
O you for whom heaven rains, lords of flowing waters and of nourishment,
you have taken your seat upon the vast chariot-seat.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you uphold the three luminous realms, the three heavens, and the three regions of space.
Increasing in strength, they protect the dominion of the Kṣatriya according to his vow, remaining unaging.
O Varuṇa, your milch-cows are full of nourishment; O Mitra, your rivers yield honey-sweet milk.
Three brilliant bulls stand as the bestowers of seed for the three worlds.

At dawn I call aloud to the goddess Aditi; at midday and at the rising of the sun, O Mitra and Varuṇa, for the sake of wealth, for complete well-being, and for the health and prosperity of our children and descendants.
You two, O Ādityas, are the upholders of the luminous realm of space, both of heaven and of earth.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, even the immortal gods do not violate your firm decrees.
For indeed, your protection extends even far and wide; O Varuṇa, O Mitra, may you now win our favor.
O you two who are free from malice, may we rightly attain that nourishment for our sustenance;
O Rudras, may we be yours.
Protect us, O Rudras, with your protections, and save us, O excellent deliverers.
May we overcome the Dasyus with our own bodies.
O you of wondrous power, may we not suffer from the malice of anyone with our bodies,
nor through our offspring, nor through our descendants.
Come to us with your great power, O Varuṇa and Mitra, destroyers of enemies,
to this beautiful sacrifice.
For you two, O Varuṇa and Mitra, are the wise rulers of all.
O sovereign lords, cause our prayers to swell with abundance. O Varuṇa and Mitra, come to us who offer oblations,
to drink of this pressed soma.
Like Atri, we invoke Mitra and Varuṇa with our songs;
sit down upon the sacred grass to drink the Soma.
By your holy law you are firm in peace; by your ordinance you bring people into harmony.
Sit down upon the sacrificial grass for the drinking of Soma. May both Mitra and Varuṇa favor our sacrifice for its fulfillment;
may they sit down upon the sacrificial grass for the drinking of Soma.

Whether you two are today in the far distance, O Aśvins, or whether you are near at hand; or whether you are in many places, O enjoyers of much, or in the mid-air—come hither! Here are those two who are most present everywhere, bringing many wondrous deeds.
I go toward the bride; I call upon the two irresistible ones, the most powerful, for my enjoyment. You have fixed one wheel of the chariot for the sake of beauty’s splendor.
With the other, you fly around the human generations and through the regions by your greatness.
Truly, this deed of yours is well performed, since all [songs] celebrate you both.
Born separately, stainless, you have entered into kinship with us. When Sūryā mounted your chariot that always speeds swiftly.
The ruddy birds surround you both, warding off the burning heat with their brilliance.
O Heroes, Atri perceives you both with a mind seeking favor, when he stirs the stainless *gharma* offering for you with his mouth, O Nāsatyas.
Fierce, towering, and swift, your chariot is heard as it moves continuously on its journeys.
O Aśvins, Heroes, when Atri turns you hither with his wondrous deeds,
the swelling, honey-loving draught of sweetness attends you, O Rudras.
When you ferry [us] across the ocean, they bring you cooked nourishments.
Truly, O Aśvins, they call you both the givers of bliss. You two, most worthy of being invoked on the journey, are the most merciful on the journey.
May these strengthening prayers be most auspicious for the Aśvins, which we have fashioned like chariots; we have uttered a great salutation.
O divine Aśvins, you who possess the wealth of thought from heaven, you are celebrated today.
Hear that, O possessors of bull-like wealth; Atri seeks to win you over.
Where are those two? Where indeed are the famous Nāsatyas, the gods in heaven?
To which people do you hasten? Or who is with you among the rivers?
To whom do you go? To whom do you approach? For whom do you yoke your chariot?
Whose prayers do you delight in? We desire you both for our protection.
For you two, O Paura and Paurāya, quicken even the one submerged in water, even the son of Pura.
When you released Cyavāna from his decrepitude— like a skin from one who has grown old— as he lay seized like a lion in the lair of the malicious;
when you made him young again, he won back the desire of his wife.
For here is your praiser; we are present for you to behold for the sake of glory.
Now hear me and come with your protections, O you who possess abundant wealth! Who among the many mortals has won you over today?
Which sage, O you who carry the sages, shall [serve] with sacrifices, O you who possess abundant wealth?
May your chariot, the swiftest among chariots, come hither, O Aśvins;
May our hymn of praise, seeking much, pass through [the crowd] among mortals.
May our praise be truly auspicious for you two who long for the sweet draught;
O wise ones, fly hither like two falcons with your winged steeds.
O Aśvins, whenever you may hear this invocation, come to us.
Excellent indeed are your enjoyments; they provide you with abundance.
O Aśvins, the R̥ṣi who praises you adorns his most beloved, powerful chariot that carries wealth with a hymn of praise. O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
Come forth, O Aśvins, beyond all people; I am the one who has won the ancient prize.
O wonder-workers, you whose paths are golden, most gracious, borne by the rivers, lovers of sweetness—hear my call! O Aśvins, come to us, bringing treasures with you both.
O Rudras, whose paths are golden, you who possess wealth and horses, lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation.
O you of excellent praise, O possessors of bovine wealth, the voice is placed upon your resonant chariot.
And your towering, wondrous beast provides nourishment; O lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation.
With awakened minds, eager for the chariot, and hearing our invocation, O Aśvins, you descend with your birds to Cyavāna, the one free from duplicity; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O heroes, your mind-yoked horses, speckled in hue, [come hither].
May the birds carry you for the drinking, together with blessings, O Aśvins; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Aśvins, come hither; O Nāsatyas, do not disregard me! Even beyond the path of the noble one, go on your circuit, O undeceivable ones; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
At this sacrifice, O undeceivable Lords of Splendor, O Aśvins, you attend to the singer who seeks your aid; O lovers of sweetness, listen to my invocation.
Dawn has appeared with her radiant cattle, and Agni, the seasonal one, has been established.
RV 5.75.9: O wonder-workers, masters of wealth, your immortal chariot has been yoked; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call! RV 5.76.1:
Agni shines forth, the face of the dawns; the god-seeking voices of the sages have arisen.
RV 5.76.2: O charioteers, come hither now toward us; O Aśvins, come toward the overflowing warm libation.
The two who travel most swiftly do not measure out their prepared course; truly, O Aśvins, you come here to this place of praise.
At the arrival of day, you are most swift to come with help, bringing most auspicious well-being to the donor who turns toward you.
And come at the time of gathering, at the early morning of the day, at midday, and at the rising of the sun!
By day and by night, with most auspicious aid, O Aśvins, let not the draught of Soma now fail you.
For this, from of old, is your place and your dwelling; these are the houses, O Aśvins, and this is our home.
From the high heaven, from the mountain, and from the waters, come to us, bringing nourishment and strength.
May we go forth with the newest, joy-bestowing aid of the Aśvins, under their excellent guidance.
Bring to us wealth, O Immortals, and heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
Worship first those two who travel at dawn; let them drink before the greedy and stingy one.
For at dawn the Aśvins receive the sacrifice; the sages praise them as those who share in the first portion.
Worship the Aśvins at dawn; urge them forward. There is no [offering] in the evening that is not pleasing to the gods.
Moreover, another besides us sacrifices; each preceding sacrificer is more successful than the one after.
Your chariot rolls forward, O Aśvins, with golden skin, honey-colored, dripping with ghee, and carrying nourishment.
Swift as thought, O Aśvins, and fleet as the wind is that chariot by which you pass over all difficulties.
He who has served the Nāsatyas most abundantly, he who gives the sweetest portion of food at the distribution.
May he protect his offspring with his peaceful aids; may he, whose radiance is not upward-turned, ever overcome [the enemy].
May we come together through the newest, joy-bestowing protection of the Aśvins, under their excellent guidance. O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
O Aśvins, come hither; O Nāsatyas, do not be averse to us.
Fly hither like two swans to the pressed soma.
O Aśvins, like two deer or like two wild oxen, come toward the pasture.
Like two swans, fly hither to the pressed juice!
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, enjoy the sacrifice for our success! Like two swans, fly hither to the pressed juice!
When Atri, descending into the *ṛbīsa*, called upon you two like a woman in her distress;
then, O Aśvins, you came with the swiftest speed of a hawk, even with a brand-new one, for our welfare.
O Lord of the Forest, gape wide open like the birth-canal of a woman about to give birth.
O Aśvins, hear my call and release Saptavadhri! For the sake of the terrified and imploring seer Saptavadhri,
O Aśvins, you two by means of your wondrous powers both joined together and tore apart the tree.
Just as the wind stirs a lotus pond from every side, so let your embryo stir; let the ten-month-old come forth.
Just as the wind, just as the forest, just as the ocean moves, so let it move.
Thus, O ten-month-old one, come forth together with the afterbirth!
Having lain for ten months within his mother,
let the boy emerge— living and uninjured— from the living woman.
O Dawn, rich in light, awaken us today for great wealth,
even as you have awakened us before for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O noble-born one, rich in horses and blessings.
O Daughter of Heaven, who have shone forth for Sunītha Śaucadratha.
May she shine forth for the most powerful Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born Dawn, rich in horses and kind favors!
Shining forth today as the bringer of wealth, dawn for us, O Daughter of Heaven!
She who has shone forth for the most powerful Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born Dawn, rich in horses and kind favors!

O Radiant One, those priests who praise you with hymns— O Bountiful Lady, they who possess great splendor, who are liberal givers of gifts, and who are noble in birth, O Mother of Horses, O Gracious One!
For even these groups of yours delight in seeking wealth.
Even the Vasatis have bestowed upon you, O noble-born Aśvasūnṛtā, gifts that are bold and worthy of giving. O wealthy Dawn, bestow upon these patrons glory accompanied by heroic sons—
upon those liberal lords who have granted us bold and noble gifts, O noble-born Aśvasūnṛtā.
Bring to them, O wealthy Dawn, great splendor and high renown— those wise patrons who bestow upon us gifts of horses and cattle, O well-born one, O giver of noble steeds!
And bring us nourishments rich in cattle, O Daughter of Heaven.
Together with the rays of the sun, with bright and glowing flames, O well-born one, rich in horses and gifts!
Shine forth, O daughter of heaven; do not delay in spreading your waters.
Lest the sun scorch you with his flame like a thief or an enemy, O well-born one, rich in horses and gifts!
O Uṣas, you ought to grant us this much, or even more— you who, O radiant one,
never fail those who praise you as you shine forth, O well-born one, rich in horses and blessings!
The lofty one whose path is brilliant, who follows the *ṛta* by means of *ṛta*, the red-hued one shining forth, full of light.
The sages praise with their hymns the goddess Uṣas as she brings forth the light of heaven. She, the beautiful one, awakening the people and making the paths easy to travel, goes at the forefront;
Great, on her vast chariot, all-inspiring, Uṣas bestows light at the beginning of days.
Yoking herself with ruddy kine, she who never fails has brought hither wealth that does not perish.
Cutting out paths for our well-being, the goddess, much-praised and possessing all boons, shines forth.
She becomes a bird of two-fold strength, revealing her body in the east.
She follows the path of *ṛta* perfectly; like one who knows the way, she does not miss the directions.
Like a bright woman conscious of her body, she has stood up as if bathing for us to behold. Driving away hatred and the darknesses, Uṣas, the daughter of Heaven, has come with light.
This daughter of heaven, turning toward men like a gracious maiden, lets her garment fall.
Unveiling desirable treasures for the donor, the youthful maiden has brought back the light as of old.
The inspired priests of the great inspired one, the wise, harness their minds and harness their thoughts.

He alone, the knower of ways, has established the priestly offices; great is the praise of the god Savitṛ. The sage puts on all forms; he has brought forth what is auspicious for bipeds and quadrupeds.
Savitṛ, the one to be chosen, has looked upon the vault of heaven; he shines along the departure of the Dawn.
After whose departure the other gods have followed, following the majesty of the god by his might;
he who measured out the earthly realms, that god Savitṛ, the steed Etaśa, by his greatness.
And you go forth, O Savitṛ, to the three luminous spheres, and you unite yourself with the rays of the sun.
And you encompass the night on both sides; and by your divine laws, O God, you become Mitra.
And you alone are the lord of procreation; and by your journeys, O God, you become Pūṣan.
And you rule over this entire world; Śyāvāśva has brought this hymn of praise to you, O Savitṛ.
We choose that nourishment of the god Savitṛ; we meditate upon the most excellent, all-sustaining, and swift bounty of Bhaga.
For of this Savitṛ there is nothing whatsoever more glorious or dearer than himself.
They do not diminish his self-sovereignty.
For he, Savitṛ, as Bhaga, impels treasures for the donor;
him we seek as a wondrous portion.
O God Savitṛ, impel for us today auspicious fortune accompanied by progeny;
drive away evil dreams.
O God Savitṛ, drive away all misfortunes.
RV_05.082.05.2 May you bring us that which is auspicious. RV_05.082.06.1 Sinless before Aditi, under the impulse of the god Savitṛ, RV_05.082.06.2 may we obtain all desirable things.
Today we choose with hymns the Lord of the True, who possesses all the gods, Savitṛ, whose impulse is truth;
he who goes before these two days, never failing.

The self-dependent god Savitṛ, who makes all these created beings hear with his song, shall impel them forth. RV_05.082.08.2 svādhīr devaḥ savitā RV_05.082.09.1 ya imā viśvā jātāny āśrāvayati ślokena RV_05.082.09.2 pra ca suvāti savitā
Speak toward him with these songs; praise the mighty one. Invite Parjanya with homage.
Bellowing like a bull that gives life-giving rain, he deposits his seed as a germ within the plants.
He strikes down the trees and he slays the demons; the entire world trembles before his great weapon.
Even the innocent man flees from the one possessed of virile power, when Parjanya, thundering, strikes down the evildoers.
Like a charioteer lashing his horses with a whip, he makes his messengers manifest; indeed, Parjanya makes the sky rain. From afar, the roars of the lion rise up when Parjanya makes the sky rain.
The winds blow forth, the lightnings fly; the plants shoot up, and the sky overflows.
Refreshing food is born for every living being when Parjanya protects the earth with his seed.
At whose command the earth bows down, at whose command the hoofed cattle spring about.
O Parjanya, under whose ordinance the plants are of every form, grant us great protection.
O Maruts, bestow rain upon us from heaven; cause the streams of the stallion to swell forth.
Come hither with this thunder, pouring down the waters, O Asura, our father.
Roar out, thunder, and deposit the germ; fly around with your water-laden chariot.
Draw forth the loosened leather bag downward; let the heights and the depths become level.
Pour down the great vessel; let the released channels flow forward.
Drench heaven and earth with clarified butter; let there be a good drinking-place for the cows.
O Parjanya, when you roar aloud and thunder, striking down the evildoers, then all this world rejoices, whatever exists upon the earth.
You have rained down rain; now lift it up and seize it! You have made the desert places passable.
You have generated the plants for our nourishment, and you have found wisdom for all living beings. Truly, O Pṛthivī, you bear the heavy burden of the mountains in this manner.
O Mighty One, you who with your greatness quicken the earth that slopes downward; O far-reaching one, the hymns of praise resound toward you through the nights.
O bright one, you who cast forth the swelling flood like a neighing steed.
She who, by her might, firmly supports even the great trees upon the earth;
when from the cloud and the lightning of heaven your rains pour down.
Sing forth a lofty and profound prayer, dear to the renowned Varuṇa, the sovereign lord.
He who, like a butcher, struck out the earth to spread it as a skin for the sun;
he stretched the atmosphere across the forests, placed speed in the horses, and milk in the cows.
Varuṇa established will in hearts, fire in the waters, the sun in heaven, and Soma on the mountain.
Varuṇa has released the water-skin with its opening turned downward toward the two worlds and the mid-air.
With that, the king of the entire world moistens the earth as rain moistens the barley.
He moistens the earth, the broad ground, and the sky, whenever Varuṇa desires the milked-out draught.
The mountains clothe themselves in cloud; the heroes, exerting their strength, relax their tension.
I shall proclaim this great, wondrous power of the renowned Varuṇa, the son of Ṛṣu:
he who, as if by measure, stands in the mid-air and has measured out the earth with the sun.
61. No one indeed has ever dared to withstand this great creative power (*māyā*) of the most wise god.
62. When the gleaming rivers, pouring forth their waters, fill the single ocean as if with water.
71. Whether it be a kinsman, O Varuṇa, or a friend, or even a brother—always [protect him].

Whether we have committed a sin against the house or against the forest, O Varuṇa, loosen that from us. Whatever the gamblers have cheated us of in the game, whether it be true or whether we do not know it—loosen all those like loosened bonds, O God; then, O Varuṇa, may we be dear to you.
O Indra and Agni, that mortal whom you both protect in battles for booty—
he shall break through even the firmest things, just as Trita split the reeds.
They who are invincible in armies and worthy of renown in contests for booty—
Indra and Agni, who have overwhelmed the five tribes—those we invoke.
Truly, the impetuous might of those two lords is fierce; their lightning-flash is sharp.
With the wooden vessel held in their hands, the slayers of Vṛtra reach out for the cattle.
O Indra and Agni, we invoke you both in this pursuit of chariots;
you two are the lords of swift bounty, the wise ones, most fond of songs of praise. Increasing day by day, O undeceivable gods, you grant prosperity to the mortal man.
I place even those two worthy ones before me, like two divine portions for the steed.
Thus has the strengthening oblation been offered to Indra and Agni, purified by the pressing-stones like clarified butter.
O you two, bestow great renown upon the patrons and wealth upon the singers; bestow nourishment upon the singers.
Let your hymns go forth to the great Viṣṇu, who is accompanied by the Maruts—the mountain-born songs, O Evayāmarut!
Let them go forth to the host that is worthy of sacrifice, the well-disposed, the powerful, the one whose gifts are praiseworthy, and to the strength whose law is to shake.
They who have been born in greatness and they who now speak of themselves through their own wisdom—O Evayāmarut!

RV_05.087.02.2 By your wisdom, O Maruts, that power of yours cannot be assailed; by their generosity and greatness, they are unassailable like the mountains. RV_05.087.03.1 They who are heard with song from the lofty heaven, brilliant and well-formed, whose march is swift—O Evayāmarut!
RV_05.087.03.2 Over whom no one has dominion in their assembly, who are like fires with their own lightning, rushing forward, the roarers of the storm.
That wide-striding one has stepped forth from the great common seat, O Evayāmarut;
when he has yoked himself by his own power upon his lofty heights, he, the fiercely contending and mighty one, comes hither with his men to increase our welfare.
Like a roar, your impetuous bull, the brilliant and swift-moving, the powerful Evayāmarut, causes all things to tremble.
RV 5.87.5: By whom they conquer and press forward, self-luminous, with firm reins, golden, well-armed, and impetuous.
RV 5.87.6: Boundless is your greatness, O ye of increased strength; let your fierce power protect us, O Evayāmarut!
For you stand as protectors in the encounter; as such, deliver us from reproach, shining like fires.

May those Rudras, the great warriors who are like fires, protect us with their abundant splendor—O Evayāmarut! The earthly seat has spread out long and wide for those whose hosts, free from offense, are great in their marches—O Evayāmarut!
O Maruts, come to us with goodwill upon your path; hear the call of the singer—O Evayāmarut!
With one accord, ward off from us the hostilities of the great Viṣṇu, as charioteers ward off with their wondrous deeds; drive away our enemies to a distance.

O you who are worthy of sacrifice, come to our well-prepared sacrifice; hear our call, O you who are without guile, O you whose march is swift! Like the highest mountains in the sky, may you, O wise ones, be difficult for the reviler to overcome.
